title: Barcelona passed on the chance to sign Chelsea ace to prioritize Gordon and Alvarez – report
description: Barcelona have spent the summer transfer window signing Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United and Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.They have also been very keen on signing Julian Alvarez from Atlet...
fullText:
Barcelona have spent the summer transfer window signing Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United and Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

They have also been very keen on signing Julian Alvarez from Atletico Madrid, with the Argentine emerging as Deco and Hansi Flick's dream striker target.

Barça have still not given up hope of signing the 26-year-old striker, with Deco in Madrid to hold talks with the player's camp and devise a strategy.

Now, according to journalist Joaquim Piera on SPORT, Barcelona had a genuine opportunity to sign Joao Pedro before Chelsea closed the door on a possible summer departure.

The Catalan club instead directed their resources towards Anthony Gordon and continued working on a move for Julian Alvarez.

Barcelona could have signed Joao Pedro in June. (Photo by Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images for AELTC, Wimbledon)

Chelsea were prepared to negotiate in June, with a deal potentially possible for around €80 million plus €20 million in variables.

However, Deco prioritised strengthening the left wing after Raphinha's injury problems created uncertainty around the position.

Barcelona eventually spent €80 million on Gordon, who is expected to compete with the Brazilian rather than simply replace Marcus Rashford in the squad.

Gordon's ability to operate as a false nine also gave Hansi Flick another tactical option. Even so, he is not a natural long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski.

Barça had identified Alvarez as their priority striker option, but it is well into August and the club have still not signed the Argentine attacker.

Alvarez remains the priority target. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Joao Pedro is close to signing an improved contract at Chelsea set to run until 2033. Arsenal also explored a transfer for the Brazilian, but the Blues did not want to strengthen a direct London rival.

For Barcelona, they made a calculated gamble by not signing the Chelsea striker, and that does not seem to have panned out well so far.

However, if the club manage to go on and sign Alvarez, the decision not to pursue a move for Joao Pedro will look smart in hindsight.

The next few weeks will determine whether Barça made a smart decision by not signing Joao Pedro or whether it will go down as a missed opportunity.

title: Dortmund send scout to observe Zagłębie Lubin gem Regula

fullText:
According to meczyki.pl, Borussia Dortmund's chief scout Bastian Schulz was conducting some research in the Polish topflight last week.

Schulz attended Legia Warsaw's 3-1 victory over Zagłębie Lubin on Sunday to observe attacking midfielder Marcel Regula.

Regula's employer confirmed to the Polish sports portal that the Westphalian giants are intrigued by the 19-year-old talent.

Meanwhile, Sky Germany also reported several days ago that fellow Bundesliga side 1.FC Köln were also keen to sign the youngster.

It's clear that if Borussia Dortmund goes ahead with the deal for the midfielder, Köln won't be able to compete financially.

However, the Cathedral City club might be able to offer the young professional more playing time compared to a competitive BVB squad.

Besides Dortmund and Effzeh, a number of other clubs from around the European continent have Regula on their radar.

title: Carlos Alcaraz’s Cincinnati withdrawal confirmed as injury concerns grow ahead of US Open
description: The No. 2 ranked men’s tennis star will not be participating in the Cincinnati Open due to a wrist injury that is set to keep him out.
fullText:
The No. 2 ranked men's tennis star will not be participating in the Cincinnati Open due to a wrist injury that is set to keep him out.

Carlos Alcaraz is arguably the biggest star in tennis at the moment. The Spaniard is ranked No. 2 in the ATP rankings, behind reigning Wimbledon champion Jannik Sinner.

Alcaraz and Sinner have quickly established themselves as the main men in the current scene. However, they haven't clashed at the highest level in a while, with Carlos missing both the French Open and Wimbledon.

The 23-year-old has spent most of 2026 recovering from a wrist injury. And just as he was set to make his return to ramp up ahead of the US Open, Alcaraz has suffered another setback.

One of the oldest tennis tournaments in the United States, the Cincinnati Open is generally a great precursor for the US Open, which is set to follow later in August.

For Alcaraz, it would have been an excellent launching pad as he makes his return from injury. However, it seems that won't be happening this year.

"Carlos Alcaraz has withdrawn from the Cincinnati Open," the tournament's official handle announced on X. "Wishing all the best to our 2025 champion in his recovery process. Can't wait to welcome you next year!

Alcaraz won the competition last year, and indeed, went on to win the US Open as well, defeating Sinner in four sets in the final.

With the Spaniard unable to participate, fans are worrying this will lead to him being unable to defend yet another major title. Hopefully, Alcaraz will still be able to make it back in time for the big one.

title: ‘LeBron, do you have any desire to be a woman?’: Donald Trump reveals plans as WNBA coach
description: Donald Trump has felt strongly about basketball as of late. The President recently weighed in on one of the longest-lasting debates going on in sports circles: who the greatest basketball player of all time is. While it’s widely viewed as a two-horse race between Michael Jordan and LeBron James, Trump made it clear that for…
fullText:
Donald Trump has felt strongly about basketball as of late. The President recently weighed in on one of the longest-lasting debates going on in sports circles: who the greatest basketball player of all time is. While it's widely viewed as a two-horse race between Michael Jordan and LeBron James, Trump made it clear that for him, it's a fairly easy choice.

"Well, Michael Jordan is a guy that's a friend of mine. He's a really good guy," Trump said during a press conference following James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers for his 24th season in the NBA. "And I think LeBron… Maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump. I don't know. I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way."

The NBA isn't the only basketball league the President has been following, either. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed that the President has been following the controversy surrounding WNBA guard Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever, who sparked debate when she said in a profile that she thinks it's important to keep transgender girls from competing in the same sports as other girls.

"I don't believe he (President Trump) has reached out to her. I know he is following the story. As you know, this is something the president feels strongly about as well, and the American people do, too: that men should not be playing in women's sports," Leavitt said.

"It's completely ludicrous that anyone could support that. It's even more ludicrous you have Sophie Cunningham, a female athlete herself, very accomplished in her own right, coming forth and speaking that truth that men shouldn't play in women's sports — we want to protect women and girls — and the backlash she is receiving from Democrats and left-wing fingers across the country is astonishing. They are clearly very out of touch with the American public on this issue."

Now, the President has linked his James-Jordan feelings and his take on trans athletes in the WNBA.

"I'd be the greatest women's basketball coach in history because I don't like LeBron James," Trump said in a public address, "I like Michael Jordan much better. But I'd go up to LeBron James.

“I’d be the greatest women’s basketball coach in history. I don’t like LeBron James, I like Michael Jordan much better. But, I’d go up to LeBron James…I’d say, ‘LeBron, did you ever have any desire to be a woman? Because what I’d love you to do is star on my team.” pic.twitter.com/xU5lt6hPeH

"It doesn't matter, I'd say, 'LeBron, did you ever have any desire to be a woman? Because what I'd love you to do is star on my team that I'm building up.' I will have the greatest team in history. They'll never lose. Nobody will come within 70 points of this team. Now, we have to change that, and we have to make it okay to talk about it."

It's an odd thing to say considering that the WNBA doesn't have a single transgender player in it, and no transgender athletes are dominating at the highest levels of college basketball either. The one transgender female basketball player that anti-trans advocates have used as an example recently, Julien Tetart, hasn't even reached the highest level of professional basketball in France

title: Luis likes Ipswich's long-term plan
description: Ipswich Town have completed the signing of Florentino Luís from Burnley, with the midfielder stating the club's long-term thinking was key in attracting him.  The 26-year-old - who already offers Premier League experience - has signed a five-year deal at Portman Road, joining for an undisclosed fee.  "It feels brilliant to be a part of this club," Florentino said.
fullText:
Ipswich Town have completed the signing of Florentino Luís from Burnley, with the midfielder stating the club's long-term thinking was key in attracting him.

The 26-year-old - who already offers Premier League experience - has signed a five-year deal at Portman Road, joining for an undisclosed fee.

"It feels brilliant to be a part of this club," Florentino said.

"I think I will be very happy here. I like how the club sees the future and there are a lot of good players here. How the club is thinking to the long-term is one of the main reasons I came here.

"I can bring experience and balance to the team, between defence and attack, and I like to bring the connection.

"Now I have signed I can't wait to meet my teammates and the fans and get started with the team."

Luis made close to 200 appearances for Benfica before joining Burnley and on bolstering his midfield, Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil said: "We are delighted to have added Florentino to the group.

"He is a player who brings experience of playing in the Premier League as well as other major competitions in Europe, including the Champions League, and makes us stronger in central midfield.

"He brings quality off the ball, as well as on it, and we look forward to him joining up with the squad."

title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders ranked as the worst veteran QB in the NFL; key reasons revealed
description: Cleveland Browns’ presumed QB1 Shedeur Sanders was ranked 35th out of the 35 eligible veteran QBs coming into the 2026-27 NFL season. Sanders had to fight his way to earn a starting role as the Browns’ QB over Dillon Gabriel last season, with this season’s battle also including veteran DeShaun Watson.
fullText:
Cleveland Browns' presumed QB1 Shedeur Sanders was ranked 35th out of the 35 eligible veteran QBs coming into the 2026-27 NFL season.

Sanders had to fight his way to earn a starting role as the Browns' QB over Dillon Gabriel last season, with this season's battle also including veteran DeShaun Watson.

Unfortunately, Sanders isn't going to enter next season as a rated QB, with executives and coaches clearly carrying a low opinion of the 24-year-old.

The Athletic's tier list survey of all 35 eligible veteran QBs saw Sanders rank dead-last, with some scathing comments from the respondents.

"He's inaccurate at all three levels," an exec said. "I can't tell if he is going to get better, but there's a huge gap between him and competent QB play."

"He's not an on-time player, can't really read through the coverages, is a little bit heavy-footed," one coordinator said. "He is thicker and harder to tackle than expected, but you shouldn't lose to him."

"I'd sleep like a baby if I got to play him every week," one defensive coordinator said.

While some recognized that Sanders could have upside under new head coach Todd Monken, they believe his existing performances rank him firmly as the worst of the bunch.

Sanders went 3-4 as a starter at the end of the season, going 120/212 on passes with a 56.6% completion and a below-average 68.1 passer rating.

Sanders' rival for the Browns' QB1 spot, Watson, ranked 31st in the same list. Sanders ranked behind quarterbacks like Minnesota Vikings' under-pressure J.J. McCarthy.

The upside is that Sanders literally has no other place to go but up heading into next season. He is getting most of the QB1 reps during the Browns' training camp.

Shedeur took all the first team reps during day six of Browns training camp, going 21/25 while Watson went 5/11.

It does look like the Browns will take the developmental risk of starting Sanders and having a veteran backup like Watson step in if Sanders isn't up to the task.

Dillon Gabriel will also factor in if neither of the QBs ahead of him can secure their spot.

The Browns haven't confirmed who their QB1 for the season will be, but all indicators point to Sanders right now.

title: Barcelona await PSG offer for 26-year-old forward as doubts over future grow
description: According to SPORT, FC Barcelona are preparing for what could be a decisive week in Ferran Torres’ future, with growing expectations inside the club that Paris Saint-Germain will submit an official ...
fullText:
According to SPORT, FC Barcelona are preparing for what could be a decisive week in Ferran Torres' future, with growing expectations inside the club that Paris Saint-Germain will submit an official offer for the Spanish forward.

Although Ferran has not directly informed the club of any desire to leave, conversations with people close to the player have led Barça to believe that a move from PSG could arrive in the coming days, possibly even before the winger returns for pre-season on August 12.

The La Liga champions have no intention of forcing Ferran out, but they are equally clear that he will only be sold if a significant offer arrives.

So far, no formal negotiations have begun between the two clubs, but Barcelona are prepared for that to change quickly.

If PSG want to sign the 26-year-old, they will need to meet the club's financial expectations.

Barcelona were surprised by Ferran's recent public remarks, particularly his statement that the club must "show they want me."

PSG want Ferran. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Within the club, those comments have been interpreted as a sign that the player may already be leaning towards a departure.

Barcelona had already informed Ferran that discussions over a new contract would not begin until September because of salary cap restrictions, following the same approach taken with other players such as Eric Garcia.

The expectation was that both sporting director Deco and head coach Hansi Flick would sit down with the player after his return from holiday to discuss his future.

However, there is now a feeling that PSG want to accelerate the process before those conversations take place.

Despite Ferran entering the final year of his contract, Barcelona are not willing to lower their demands.

The Catalans believe the striker market is extremely limited, while Ferran's value has risen following his performances at the World Cup.

If PSG fail to meet their asking price, the Blaugrana are prepared to keep the player for the entire season, even if that creates the risk of losing him on a free transfer in 2027.

Barcelona believe Ferran's representatives have been in discussions with PSG for some time and that personal terms may not be an obstacle if the French champions decide to move forward.

Likely to leave. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Should the player ultimately decide against leaving, the Catalans remain willing to offer him a contract extension later this year, although the proposal would include no major salary increase.

While the club value Ferran's contribution, neither the sporting department nor Hansi Flick currently view him as an untouchable player within the project.

If Ferran eventually departs, Barcelona are expected to reinvest in a new centre-forward.

Julian Alvarez remains the club's primary target, and Barcelona intend to pursue him until the end of the transfer window.

Should that move prove impossible, the club have already identified two alternative striker profiles capable of strengthening the attack.

title: Falcons edge Jalon Walker carted off practice field with leg injury

fullText:

Jalon Walker, the second-year defensive edge out of the University of Georgia, went down with a leg injury. He had to be carted off the field.

title: Liverpool enter club to club talks to sign England international
description: Liverpool have entered club to club talks to sign an England international. Richard Hughes is rapidly running out of time to rescue what is becoming an increasingly uncomfortable transfer window.There...
fullText:
Liverpool have entered club to club talks to sign an England international.

Richard Hughes is rapidly running out of time to rescue what is becoming an increasingly uncomfortable transfer window.

There is still a chance to turn things around before the deadline, but as things stand, there is a growing feeling that Andoni Iraola is being asked to perform miracles with an unbalanced squad.

Nobody expected the new Liverpool head coach to inherit a perfect team. That much was obvious the moment he walked through the door. The expectation, however, was that Hughes would use the summer to reshape the squad around Iraola's demanding, high-intensity style of football.

Instead, Liverpool have spent much of the window pursuing Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande. Diomande has now rejected a move to Anfield, while Paris Saint-Germain continue to hold firm over Barcola's valuation. Liverpool may yet land one of their priority targets, but the drawn-out pursuit has come at a cost.

While attention has been fixed on signing another winger, glaring weaknesses elsewhere in the squad remain.

With just over two weeks until the Premier League season begins, Liverpool's defensive depth already looks alarmingly thin.

Joe Gomez and Jeremy Jacquet are both sidelined with injuries, Giovanni Leoni is still working his way back from the ACL injury that ended his previous campaign, and Conor Bradley faces another spell on the sidelines after suffering yet another fitness setback.

The result is that Iraola has spent pre-season patching together makeshift defensive units rather than building the partnerships and understanding that every new manager desperately needs. Pre-season should be about implementing ideas and creating cohesion. Instead, Liverpool have simply been trying to get enough defenders onto the pitch.

Right now, Virgil van Dijk is the only senior centre-back fully available.

Youngsters have stepped up admirably. Ifeanyi Ndukwe has impressed throughout pre-season and shown he looks comfortable at the level. Unfortunately, he is unlikely to remain at Anfield this season because he does not currently satisfy the work permit requirements and is expected to head out on loan. Mor Talla Ndiaye and Luke Chambers have also been handed opportunities, but both are naturally more comfortable on the left side of the defence.

Things should improve once players return. Jacquet's injury is not thought to be serious, Gomez is edging closer to fitness and Leoni should soon be back in full training.

But should Liverpool really be relying on that?

Gomez's injury record makes him difficult to count on across a full campaign, while both Jacquet and Leoni are completely untested in the Premier League and are themselves returning from injuries. That is hardly the foundation of a title-chasing defence.

The concerns extend beyond the centre of defence too. Bradley's fitness problems are becoming an unfortunate pattern, having missed more than 20 matches through injury in each of his three seasons with the first team.

Jeremie Frimpong offers an attacking alternative, but asking him to play as a traditional right-back every week would take away many of the qualities that make him such an exciting player.

Liverpool still need another winger. That much is obvious. But the longer this window goes on, the clearer it becomes that the defensive rebuild deserves just as much attention.

If Hughes fails to address it before the season begins, Iraola could find himself fighting with one hand tied behind his back before a competitive ball has even been kicked.

It looks like the club's sporting director is working on it though. TuttoJuve claim that England international Fikayo Tomori has ended up on Liverpool's radar as they look to bring in an experienced centre-back.

The report goes as far to say that Liverpool have even initiated exploratory club to club talks with AC Milan in order to determine how feasible a move would be.

So, it looks like Tomori is one to keep an eye on.

title: Wonderkid confirms he is about to replace Kostas Tsimikas
description: An exciting wonderkid will replace Kostas Tsimikas this summer. The Greek scouser has been a beloved character at Anfield over the years. Tsimikas is the best kind of player to have in a squad that is...
fullText:
An exciting wonderkid will replace Kostas Tsimikas this summer.

The Greek scouser has been a beloved character at Anfield over the years. Tsimikas is the best kind of player to have in a squad that is looking to compete on all fronts.

He may have never become a starter but during his six years at the club he has played a key role in Liverpool's successes. Whether under Jurgen Klopp or Arne Slot, Liverpool could not have had a better understudy to Andy Robertson as Tsimikas.

Arriving from Olympiakos, Tsimikas was able to step into Robertson's shoes in any situation. Both in the League Cup and the FA Cup, Tsimikas played a key role. Meanwhile, he was also a pretty solid player in the Premier League as well making well over 50 appearances for the Reds in the league.

Tsimikas' delivery and his tenacious defending has been the highlight of his game. But it's clear that Liverpool are now moving on from the Greek international.

Last summer's acquisition of Milos Kerkez confirmed that. Tsimikas was then ultimately loaned and didn't have a great time at AS Roma.

He struggled to get into the Italian side's squad and he's not caught the eye in pre-season under Andoni Iraola either.

At 30-years-old, Tsimikas is reaching the final years of his career. He will want to bow out on a high and it's also important to note that Liverpool probably can't afford to give one of their precious non-homegrown spots to a player who likely won't be playing an awful lot considering he is merely Kerkez's back-up.

That was fine when Tsimikas was in the prime of his career. But now Liverpool need a more astute back-up, someone who can push Kerkez and someone who can step-up and be recognised as the future of the club.

It's why even though there aren't a lot of rumours about his departure, it's pretty much guaranteed at this stage that Tsimikas is going to leave.

Liverpool need more additions in the squad and they need to free-up non-homegrown spaces, currently there are only two available spaces and that is before counting the addition of Bradley Barcola.

So while the Reds have been quiet about it, it's pretty obvious that Iraola has the perfect plan staring directly at him.

One exciting youngster confirmed it with his performances in pre-season.

Because sure enough if Tsimikas leaves, he will need to be replaced. Just relying on Kerkez alone to play the left-back slot won't be enough.

Sure, Joe Gomez can also play there, but ask yourself, when was the last time he even started five consecutive games in a row? Gomez simply cannot be relied upon.

And therein lies Liverpool's problem. The lack of depth in defence isn't just at full-back, it's everywhere. Which is why Liverpool want versatile defenders.

And that is why Luke Chambers confirmed he is about to become Tsimikas' replacement with his performances in pre-season. Chambers is a club-trained player. He counts as homegrown and he can also play as a centre-back not just as a left-back.

He showcased that against Wrexham and Leeds United, even scoring against the latter. Chambers is clearly a very good defender and he's proven he can play at a high level.

At 22-years-old, given the fact that he is homegrown as well and Liverpool's need to have a defender capable of playing multiple roles, Chambers is the obvious choice to replace Tsimikas.

title: Real Madrid set historic transfer record as academy sales fund Mourinho’s rebuild – report
description: Real Madrid have had an unprecedented transfer window so far, bringing in the likes of Denzel Dumfries, Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Carlos Espi.Los Blancos are also working to ...
fullText:
Real Madrid have had an unprecedented transfer window so far, bringing in the likes of Denzel Dumfries, Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konate and Carlos Espi.

Los Blancos are also working to sign the talented Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig and Rodri from Manchester City.

However, this transfer window has been remarkable not just for the signings Los Blancos have made but also for the sales they have managed.

Now, according to AS, this summer has already become the most profitable in Real Madrid's history for player sales.

The departures of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios to Fulham have taken Los Blancos' total income from outgoing transfers to a remarkable €189 million, surpassing the club's previous record and underlining the enormous value of La Fabrica.

Real Madrid sold Gonzalo to Fulham for €40 million. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Every euro of the €189 million generated this summer has come from players developed by Real Madrid or those with strong academy ties.

The biggest sale remains Nico Paz's €60 million move to Como, while Gonzalo Garcia's €40 million transfer to Fulham is now the second-largest departure of the window.

Victor Munoz (€20.5 million), Mario Gila (€15 million), Alvaro Rodriguez (€12.5 million), Alex Jimenez (€12.5 million), Cesar Palacios (€10 million) and several other academy graduates have also contributed to the record-breaking figure.

The €189 million figure may not be the final total.

Real Madrid are still working on several outgoing deals, including Fulham's interest in Thiago Pitarch, Strasbourg's pursuit of Jacobo Ortega and a potential transfer involving Sergio Arribas, from which the club would receive 50 percent of the transfer fee thanks to a sell-on agreement.

Thiago Pitarch could still leave Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Should those deals materialise, the club are expected to comfortably surpass the €200 million mark before the transfer window closes.

The timing of those sales is significant, as it has allowed Jose Mourinho to make the signings he needs to build his new project.

Rather than placing massive pressure on the board to fund signings, La Fabrica sales have directly helped the club reinforce the first team.

Real Madrid have always used this model successfully, but this summer transfer window is the pinnacle of that philosophy.

If Los Blancos go on to have a memorable 2026-27 season, these sales would have to be remembered as one of the main launchpads on which the project was built.

It remains to be seen how much the Merengues are able to increase that figure between now and the end of the summer transfer window.

We can't say we're not a little disappointed that Jose Mourinho's men are poised to win a hard-fought battle for Diomande's services.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

When we look at a winger market that's apparently dominated by left-sided options, the RB Leipzig sensation stood out as the obvious choice to fill Mo Salah's shoes following the Egyptian's early departure.

Alas, it was not to be, with the Merseysiders instead moving for the next elite option on the list in the versatile (but primarily left-sided) Bradley Barcola.

With the right-sided Mbaye (although unfortunately right-footed) also understood to have caught the eye at the AXA training centre, this would still leave Liverpool in a promising situation on both flanks.

We have to emphasise that Liverpool haven't done themselves any favours with their seismic drop-off in form in 2025/26.

But still, there would probably be some underlying concern over Yan Diomande's loyalty to the cause at some point, given how quickly he's shifted allegiance between Liverpool, PSG and Real Madrid in the space of a year.

Would we have been at risk of becoming embroiled in another transfer saga a year or two down the line if one of PSG or Madrid took a liking to the Ivory Coast international? Quite possibly.

Mind, it's a risk one takes with any elite (or elite potential) footballer.

Nonetheless, It's a missed opportunity we feel we can live with – provided Liverpool can get deals for Mbaye and Barcola over the line this summer.

Oh, and while we're at it, backup for Alexander Isak wouldn't go amiss either.

title: Chelsea nearing £16.3m deal for Rayo defender Chavarria
description: Chelsea are closing in on an agreement with Rayo Vallecano for defender Pep Chavarria.
fullText:
Chelsea are closing in on an agreement with Rayo Vallecano for defender Pep Chavarria.

The Blues, who have already agreed personal terms with the 28-year-old, are finalising a move worth about £16.3m plus further add-ons, with all parties increasingly confident about striking a deal.

Left-back Chavarria is a key target for new manager Xabi Alonso having faced him while he was in charge of Real Madrid last season.

It has been almost a month since Chelsea had an initial £15m bid rejected by the La Liga club when talks began at the end of June.

Negotiations became protracted amid a belief at Chelsea that Rayo were raising their valuation during the process, asking as much as the full £42.8m release clause at one stage.

Chavarria made it clear to Rayo, who lost to Crystal Palace in the Conference League final in May, that he wanted to move to Stamford Bridge.

Alongside new right-back Marco Palestra, who joined Chelsea for £47m from Atalanta in July, Chavarria's arrival would give Alonso the chance to replicate his wing-back system that helped Bayer Leverkusen win the Bundesliga title in 2024.

His signing also adds depth to the left-back position after Marc Cucurella joined Real Madrid in June for £51.8m.

It is also another player with experience added to the squad, along with the signings of striker Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton and Jordan Henderson, 36, after he cancelled his contract with Brentford.

Chelsea have also signed club-record £117m forward Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa and defender Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace for £52m, with midfielder Valentin Barco expected to join from partner club Strasbourg imminently.

They are expected to focus on player sales in the coming weeks having reached an agreement to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Italian club Como 1907 for about £31m.

Premier League clubs Tottenham Hotspur and Everton are both preparing offers for Galatasaray winger Baris Alper Yilmaz, according to Sporx. Roberto De Zerbi and David Moyes are at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Hill Dickinson Stadium with the Toffees.

Adding to the complexity is a 20% sell-on clause held by his former club Ankara Keciorengucu, meaning Galatasaray must negotiate a premium fee to maximise their net profit.

Tottenham are keen to bolster their attack with players who suit Roberto De Zerbi's high-intensity style. While a move for Manchester City's Savinho remains the top priority, Yilmaz's ability to drive forward with power and stretch opposition defences makes him an appealing fit for Spurs.

Meanwhile, Everton are actively seeking high-impact reinforcements to strengthen their squad and add quality out wide as they look to maintain their push for European qualification.

Both clubs have made initial verbal enquiries and are expected to formalise their interest with concrete proposals in the coming days.

fullText:
More than two months after his final game for Liverpool, Mo Salah is reportedly on the cusp of joining a new club.

The Egyptian bade an emotional farewell to Anfield at the end of last season, bowing out as the Reds' third-highest goalscorer of all time (257 goals) and universally recognised as one of the club's greatest ever players.

There's been an abundance of speculation as to where the 34-year-old might go next after calling time on his LFC career, and there now seems to be clarity in that regard.

On Monday night, Fabrizio Romano took to X to report that Salah is bound for Turkish Super Lig outfit Trabzonspor, who finished third in their domestic league last season.

The Italian posted: 'BREAKING: Mo Salah to Trabzonspor, here we go! Club confirms agreement in place for the Egyptian striker. Salah joins on two-year deal as free agent after leaving Liverpool.'

Ben Jacobs subsequently claimed (via X) that the 34-year-old is due to arrive in Istanbul today and continue on to Trabzon this evening, with the transfer set to be 'formalised' later in the week.

Salah's reported choice of destination might seem surprising, considering that he'd have surely had his pick of elite European clubs, or a lucrative suitor from the Saudi Pro League.

However, by agreeing a deal with Trabzonspor, he'll be playing in a competitive domestic division for a club who are also participating in the Europa League this coming season, with a play-off round to navigate prior to the group stage.

That'd ensure that the Liverpool legend is still operating at a reasonably high level, rather than merely accepting an 'easy' option to see out the final few years of his illustrious career.

It'll feel strange not seeing Salah rampaging along the right flank at Anfield over the coming months, and the hierarchy in L4 continue their quest to replace him, with Paris Saint-Germain duo Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye both being sought.

title: Elite climber Falconer chasing 2028 Olympic dream
description: Bouldering helped Mary Falconer deal with the loss of her mother and could also set her on the path to becoming an Olympian.
fullText:
Mary Falconer is your typical shy teenager, and clearly uncomfortable in front of a camera.

But put her on a boulder wall, like the one we find ourselves on at Flashpoint Swansea, and the 15-year-old is transformed.

Watching her confidently glide up the holds - and seemingly defy physics - it is hard to think this elite athlete was once what her father Richard describes as the "little girl who refused to go for a walk".

And perhaps what is even more remarkable, Falconer only took up bouldering three years ago as a way to cope with the death of her mother Anca to a rare cancer.

"It's helped me a lot mentally because you can put all your emotions into the wall and into your training," she said.

Falconer, from Haverfordwest, now finds herself as one of the top youth climbers in the UK and boasts multiple national and regional podium finishes.

She travels all over the UK and Europe following her passion, with the ultimate goal of competing at the 2028 Olympics, which she says "would be a dream come true".

But Falconer, who was selected for the England squad during her first year of competition, wants to represent her mother's native Romania at the Games.

"It would be great, I'd really love to do it," she said.

"They [Romania's coaches] have been great, they've given me a lot of support so far and have taken me on quite quickly."

Falconer has already been accepted by the Romanian team and will compete in two European climbing events this summer, alongside Romania's national championships later in the year.

Falconer was first introduced to climbing at a wakeboarding park near Narberth.

Her father, a keen wakeboarder himself, tried to get her on the water, but Falconer admits she did not like the cold and headed indoors to the bouldering gym.

"I fell in love with it straight away," she said.

"You can progress every day and it's really satisfying to see.

"It's definitely taken a lot of hard work, lots of training in the gym and climbing almost every day."

Such is Falconer's dedication, Richard built a gym in their home where it is not unusual for his daughter to be training until the early hours of the morning.

While the banging of weights above his bedroom causes a few sleepless nights, Richard says "it's a privilege" to be in his situation.

"It's a huge responsibility, a lot of work, but why would you not support this? She's doing amazing things," he said.

Richard, who has worked in many sectors including the military, admits he has never seen a work ethic like it.

"I've never once ever said 'you need to do this, or you should work harder at this', all of it is driven by herself," he said.

Falconer's mother Anca died when Mary was just seven years old, leaving Richard with the unenviable task of raising a grieving daughter.

"We worked very hard at fixing the situation, reinventing us, our relationship, revisiting places we'd gone on holiday as a family, desensitising those situations, but there was always an element that couldn't be fixed," he said.

"What sport gave her was a way of expressing and, in return, she got positive affirmation back from the people she was climbing with. It gave her something that she was the owner of, a responsibility.

"So sports fixed the last 20% of Mary, gave her focus, gave her purpose, and put her on a trajectory that, who knows, the Olympics - the sky's the limit."

Falconer, who has dual nationality, is very close with her Romanian grandmother and visits three to four times a year.

"She's really the only family we have and to have Mary climb for Romania and give her grandmother and great grandmother that element of pride - they just live for her," said Richard.

And her fanbase is not just limited to family, Falconer is often stopped at competitions and asked for selfies and autographs.

"It always puts a smile on my face, it's definitely motivating to see young girls inspired," said Falconer, whose well-documented climbing journey has a staggering social media reach of over 1.7 million impressions every month.

So it would seem the shy girl small town girl will have to get used to the cameras, and soon.

title: Tua Tagovailoa on training camp with Michael Penix: "It's definitely a competition"
description: Both of the Falcons' quarterbacks are limited with injuries, but Tagovailoa says that isn't stopping them from competing.
fullText:
Falcons quarterbacks Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix are both limited by injuries in training camp, but that isn't stopping them from competing for the starting job.

Tagovailoa said on NFL Network that while he rests an injured back and Penix rehabs the torn ACL he suffered in November, they continue to compete.

"I view it as a competition. I understand he can't take some team reps right now because of what he's going through, but he's still being able to compete in seven-on-seven, he's still able to go through some plays," Tagovailoa said. "It's definitely a competition."

Tagovailoa said his own back injury won't limit him for much longer.

"Nothing too serious, just a caution kind of thing where we're not rushing it. It was just a flare-up, nothing big, not anything long-term. We'll be fine," Tagovailoa said.

The Falcons have to hope at least one of their quarterbacks will be 100 percent when they open the season on September 13 against the Steelers.

title: Kenneth Walker addresses Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy’s absence from training camp after personal tragedy
description: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III shared his feelings on OC Eric Bieniemy’s absence from training camp. Bieniemy is dealing with a significant personal issue after a shooting at his house left his wife injured and his son in custody.
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III shared his feelings on OC Eric Bieniemy's absence from training camp.

Bieniemy is dealing with a significant personal issue after a shooting at his house left his wife injured and his son in custody.

The OC is crucial to the Chiefs' hopes for any title success this season, with Walker making his feelings on the situation clear.

Walker made it clear that he can't wait for Bieniemy to return from his situation while promising that the team will stay locked in until he can join them.

"Prayers to his family. We'll hold it down. When he gets back, we're ready to have that intensity and that energy. You can't take a play off because he is going to say something to you about it."

Walker joined the Chiefs in free agency and was excited to be coached by the legendary OC, but those plans had to be put on hold for a much bigger reason.

Bieniemy will also be excited to have Walker as an offensive weapon, with him coming into the season as the reigning Super Bowl MVP with the Seattle Seahawks.

Walker put up 1,027 rushing yards and 5 touchdowns with 31 receptions, 282 receiving yards, and 0 touchdowns last season, eyeing a potentially big season in Kansas City under Bieniemy and Andy Reid.

On July 26, 2026, Eric Bieniemy's wife, Mia (age 57), was shot multiple times at the family's home in the 20000 block of Northpark Drive in Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia.

She was shot twice with a .22-caliber Ruger firearm: once in the left forearm and once in the left shoulder, undergoing surgery for her injuries, but survived the ordeal.

Their son, Elijah Zion Bieniemy (age 27), was arrested and charged with malicious wounding, use of a firearm in the commission of a felony, and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling.

Elijah's public defender stated he 'appears to suffer from significant mental health issues,' although there's no formalized diagnosis. No motive has been revealed for the incident either.

Eric Bieniemy has no timetable to return to the Chiefs currently, serving as the primary caregiver to their son, Eric Bieniemy III, who has cerebral palsy, as Mia recovers.

title: Wenger statement puts distance between himself and Infantino
description: Arsene Wenger has come under fire for standing by and allowing FIFA to “sell” the World Cup, which has forced the Arsenal icon to distance himself from the proposal.Wenger has been working at FIFA...
fullText:
Arsene Wenger has come under fire for standing by and allowing FIFA to "sell" the World Cup, which has forced the Arsenal icon to distance himself from the proposal.

Wenger has been working at FIFA since leaving his role as Arsenal manager in 2018 and appears to play an important role within the organisation. This meant many believed proposals of that nature would have passed through him and that he should have stopped them before they reached the public domain.

However, that did not happen and FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under serious pressure to resign following the controversial proposal. Other FIFA officials who did not step down and were perceived to have allowed or supported the proposal have also faced significant criticism in recent days.

Wenger has been among those criticised, but he has now explained his role within the organisation to make it clear that he was never involved in the proposal when it was drafted.

He said, as reported by Give Me Sport:

"The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side.

"At FIFA, I am the Chief of Global Football Development.

"Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world.

"In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger's statement was intended to clarify his responsibilities within FIFA and distance himself from the proposal. He stressed that his work focuses on football development rather than strategic planning, while reaffirming his belief in an independent FIFA that operates with commitment, transparency, and integrity.

title: Wrexham set to sign Preston captain Whiteman
description: Wrexham are poised to complete the signing of Preston North End captain Ben Whiteman.
fullText:
Wrexham are poised to complete the signing of Preston North End captain Ben Whiteman.

The midfielder has made 200 Championship appearances and completed a medical with the Red Dragons on Tuesday.

He is now expected to become the club's second capture of the summer transfer window following the arrival of full-back Danny Imray from Crystal Palace.

Whiteman has been slammed by North End boss Paul Heckingbottom, who said the 30-year-old forced a move away from the Deepdale club.

Heckingbottom feels the experienced midfielder crossed a line by telling club bosses that he had played his final game for Preston.

"Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has," Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation.

"He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player."

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

Smith hungry for more after new Wrexham deal

US tour highlights Wrexham's stock higher than ever

Whiteman, a product of Manchester United's academy, played 43 times for Preston in the Championship last season as they finished 14th.

The Rochdale native joined Sheffield United as a teenager and made his senior debut in 2014 before spells on loan at Mansfield Town and Doncaster Rovers.

Whiteman later made his move to Doncaster permanent in 2018 and remained with Rovers, who named him captain, until 2021 when he joined Preston.

It comes as Wrexham midfielder George Dobson has been linked with a move to League One Sheffield Wednesday.

title: A broken leg ended his junior season. But Trail QB Drew McGlumphy is back under center
description: A year after a broken leg took away his junior season, Buckeye Trail's Drew McGlumphy returns to write the final chapter of his high school career.
fullText:
OLD WASHINGTON − Senior Drew McGlumphy still remembers every agonizing detail of the play.

There was no hole in the defense, so the Buckeye Trail quarterback did what he had done dozens of times during an all-state sophomore season for the Warriors — he cut back to his left. Two defenders engaged, another jumped on his back, and in a split second during an August scrimmage against John Glenn, his leg stayed pinned to the turf.

The snap that followed wasn't a center exchange. It was the sound of a Division I prospect's junior season shattering before it ever truly began.

"I remember the play pretty clearly," McGlumphy recalled. "My leg just kind of stayed where it was, and I felt it snap. I knew immediately it was broken. The pain was the worst pain I've ever felt. I remember just laying there pretty upset and thinking, 'Why me? I knew my season was over.'"

For a young QB on the brink of a breakout career, the timing was cruel. As a sophomore, McGlumphy set the Eastern District ablaze, piling up over 1,000 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards while accounting for more than 20 touchdowns in leading Buckeye Trail to the OHSAA playoffs.

McGlumphy reeled in First Team Division VI Eastern District, All OVAC, and All-IVC honors along with Division VI All-Ohio Special Mention accolades. By April, he had earned his first Division I scholarship offer from Miami of Ohio University.

More college football coaches were eager to see his junior season film. Instead, one single play wiped it all away.

"Mentally, it was one of the toughest things I've ever been through," McGlumphy said. "After everything that had happened after my sophomore year with recruiting and how pumped I was for my junior season, it felt like everything I'd worked for disappeared in one play."

While sitting out his junior season on the gridiron was a mental battle, that initial Division I interest provided a powerful light during his darkest days.

"Getting that offer was awesome," McGlumphy said. "And I'm still being recruited by Miami of Ohio and attended their camp this summer. I had several other schools showing interest before the injury. That definitely motivated me through my rehab. I wanted to get healthy so I could get back on the field and show everyone I'm back and playing at an even higher level."

When Friday nights arrived at the Baker Activity Complex without him on the field, McGlumphy took that motivation to One Body Physical Therapy and Sports Medicine in Zanesville, logging 10 to 12 hours a week under therapist Matt Amicone and his staff.

"Matt had already been helping me for about three years with speed training and my shoulder rehab, so we had built a great relationship," McGlumphy said. "He's one of the smartest people I've worked with and always knew when to push me and when to challenge me."

Rehab wasn't standard stretching — it was a high-tech effort. McGlumphy cycled through hyperbaric oxygen therapy, blood flow restriction (BFR) and red-light therapy.

"I was there 4 to 6 days a week for a couple of hours every session. Plus I worked at home every day," McGlumphy said. "Recovery became my full-time job. Every day was about getting a little bit better."

While physical therapy rebuilt his leg, emotional strength came from a close family circle.

With his older brother leaving for college just a week before the injury, it was just Drew and his parents, Mike and Mandy, at home. Suddenly, an elite quarterback who ran a 4.68 40-yard dash was completely dependent on his family for daily tasks.

"They took time off work to help me because I couldn't do much on my own," McGlumphy shared. "My dad helped me shower, my parents helped me get dressed, get around the house, and took me to doctor appointments and physical therapy almost every day."

In those quiet moments on the couch, his mindset shifted from frustration to purpose.

"My faith became a huge part of my recovery," McGlumphy said. "In the beginning, I struggled with the 'why me', but over time I learned God had a plan even when I couldn't understand it. And I had a solid support system in place helping me. I honestly don't think I'd be where I am today without my parents, Matt and his staff at One Body, my doctors, my teammates, coaches, and everyone who supported me."

Months of grueling work paid off under a loaded barbell in the weight room about two months ago. McGlumphy stepped under the squat rack and drove upward for a 415-pound squat, proving to himself that the physical battle was won.

More: New voices, high expectations as Guernsey County football hits full refresh

More: Friday Night Blueprint ∣ 2026 Week-by-Week Schedules for area high school football

"My body felt great, and I wasn't thinking about my leg anymore," McGlumphy said. "I was just lifting, and that was probably the first moment I thought, 'I'm back.'"

On the football side, after spending a year processing games from the sideline like a coach unlocked a new mental layer to his overall game.

"Personally, the game has slowed down for me," McGlumphy said. "I think I make better reads now and understand defenses better. Some of that is seeing the game in a different way last year when I was out."

That refined mental perspective comes at the perfect time. First-year Buckeye Trail head coach Devin Nicholes, who previously served on the Warriors staff during McGlumphy's freshman year has installed a more complex offense built directly around his talented quarterback's unique skill set.

"It means alot to have his trust," McGlumphy said of Nicholes. "He's willing to build the offense around the strengths of the players we have and continue expanding our playbook. Instilling a new offense isn't easy, but I'm excited to help lead it and set the standard for the younger guys coming up behind us."

That dedication hasn't gone unnoticed by the Trail coaching staff. Nicholes has watched his signal-caller orchestrate the offense without missing a beat throughout summer preparations.

"Drew has worked incredibly hard throughout the offseason to get back on the field," Nicholes said. "He's been able to do every exercise and drill at a very high level. His ability to comprehend our offense and defense allows for him to make our calls and checks while on the field."

Now fully cleared and physically stronger than ever, McGlumphy will step onto the home turf at the Baker Activity Complex for Week 1 not just as an elite playmaker, but as a leader forged through adversity.

For McGlumphy, running onto the field for his senior opening won't just mark the start of a new season — it will be the triumphant payoff of a grueling 12-month climb.

"It's hard to put into words," McGlumphy said. "A year ago, I would have done anything just to have another chance to play football. Now, I get to open my senior season at home, and that makes it even more special. Every hour of rehab, every difficult day, every setback. It all feels worth it, and I'm really thankful to be back doing what I love most."

title: Manchester City could move for Chelsea star depending on Savinho departure
description: Manchester City Open Pedro Neto Talks Over Pedro Neto TransferManchester City have made direct contact with Pedro Neto’s representatives as early discussions begin over a possible move, according to...
fullText:
Manchester City have made direct contact with Pedro Neto's representatives as early discussions begin over a possible move, according to Fabrizio Romano. The Portugal international has emerged as one of the options under consideration at the Etihad, with the situation closely tied to Savinho's future and Chelsea's valuation.

As things stand, City's interest in Neto appears conditional rather than advanced. The winger is among the names being assessed if Savinho departs for Tottenham, a development that would reshape Manchester City's plans in the wide areas. Neto is also understood to be on Tottenham's list as a fallback option, adding another layer to what could become a competitive market.

Any serious move is likely to depend on Chelsea's asking price. That part of the equation may prove decisive, especially in a market where Premier League-proven attackers command substantial fees. If no figure is stated publicly, expectations around a deal of this profile naturally point towards a significant outlay, and City are known to be measured when it comes to value.

Neto's profile fits much of what elite clubs seek. He offers direct running, pace and the ability to stretch defences from either flank. When fully fit, he has consistently shown the sort of explosiveness that can alter matches quickly, which helps explain why Manchester City and Tottenham are both monitoring the position carefully.

For City, this looks like intelligent groundwork rather than a move at full speed. Internal planning around Savinho is clearly central, and that makes sense given how interconnected modern transfer windows have become. Clubs at this level rarely act in isolation on one player when multiple squad decisions are unfolding at once.

There is also a wider strategic element. Neto would bring Premier League experience and immediate readiness, reducing the adaptation risk that often comes with overseas recruitment. Whether that becomes enough to trigger formal negotiations may rest on Chelsea softening their valuation and on Tottenham's own progress in the market.

As a slightly stunned Manchester City supporter, this report leaves me with mixed feelings. On one hand, Pedro Neto is a very good player. He is sharp, aggressive, exciting in one-v-one situations and capable of giving City something more vertical out wide. There are moments when our attack can feel a touch too structured, so a winger who thrives on chaos has obvious appeal.

On the other hand, the mention of Savinho potentially going to Spurs is the part that really jars. If that is genuinely part of the chain here, then many fans will wonder why City would allow a talented young wide player to leave, only to spend heavily on another winger. It raises fair questions about squad planning and long-term trust in younger attackers.

Then there is Chelsea's valuation. That alone could make supporters nervous, because buying from a direct rival in the Premier League rarely comes cheap. Neto has clear quality, but availability has been part of the conversation around him for a while, and fans will naturally weigh that risk against what City already have.

Still, if Enzo Maresca and the recruitment team believe Neto is the right fit, supporters will hope it is part of a bigger and sharper attacking refresh. The surprise is real, but so is the intrigue.

title: Commanders RB says Jayden Daniels is best QB he's played with, including Tom Brady
description: Rachaad White says Jayden Daniels is best QB he's played with. He played one year with Tom Brady. White explains why.
fullText:
Rachaad White wasn't messing around on Tuesday.

The NFL veteran of four seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't beat around the bush. He told the interviewer that Jayden Daniels "is the best QB I've ever played with."

RACHAAD WHITE: Jayden Daniels "is the best QB I've ever played with."

Great insights today in my conversation w/Rachaad on Commanders star QB Jayden Daniels.

Rachaad & JD5 were teammates at Arizona State before Jayden transferred to LSU. Now, the duo reunited w/the Commanders. pic.twitter.com/PdMTrcHzP6

The Commanders signed White this offseason with the hopes that he can produce productive carries as well as be their primary passing-downs running back, out of the backfield. Of course, there is one very interesting fact about this Rachaad White quote that mustn't be overlooked. You see, in White's rookie year, the quarterback for the Tampa Bay Bucs was a fella playing his last NFL season. You may have heard of him...Tom Brady.

White was at Tampa Bay during the 2022-2025 seasons, and Brady was the starting quarterback in Tampa Bay during the 2020-2022 seasons. Why would White say that Daniels is the best quarterback he has enjoyed as a teammate? Well, might there be a couple of reasons?

First, Daniels was the quarterback at Arizona State when White was a Sun Devil running back teammate. They are college buddies, and it is not unusual when young people leave home; they are much more vulnerable than they ever dared imagine or admit, thus college friendships/relationships can quickly become lifelong, whether good or bad.

Secondly, the fact that the Bucs were only 8-9 in Tom Brady's final NFL season (White's rookie season) may be helping White not to consider Brady the best quarterback as a teammate. That final season in Tampa was an odd one in the sense that the Bucs seemed to pass entirely too much. As a result, Brady led the NFL in attempts that season with 733. Although Brady also led the NFL in receptions in 2022 with 490, he finished his career with a career-low yards per passing attempt at only 6.4. BTW, it was 7.6 and 7.4 in Brady's first two Buccaneers seasons.

Thirdly, White could be referring to the fact that Daniels telephoned White one night after White's slow start to this 2026 Commanders training camp. According to White, Daniels was being a leader, checking in on White to see if he was okay, but also challenging White to meet the challenge. White received what Daniels had to say well, believing it was coming from a friend.

White claims that Daniels was the same type of person at Arizona State: the smile, the leadership, the hard work. White says he naturally followed Daniels at Arizona State, and he plans to do the same here in Washington with the Commanders. White anticipated the Brady comparison, so he got out in front of it, saying he has a lot of love for Brady, but he has been saying since he was in Tempe that Daniels is the best quarterback he has played with.

For whatever it's worth, White did say he has a lot of love for Brady, but he was saying this about Daniels before he ever played with Brady. Remember, It's all subjective, and one man's opinion, of course, but the fan base would certainly want to hear about this. So USA Today, Commanders Wire continues to provide you with our daily coverage.

title: Why is Mohamed Salah signing for Trabzonspor?
description: As Salah is a free agent, Trabzonspor would have needed to commit to covering the Egyptian’s enormous wages - but the Liverpool icon also offers huge commercial upside
fullText:
Mohamed Salah has chosen his next club: Turkish side Trabzonspor.

The Liverpool icon, who left Anfield as a free agent at the end of last season, has arrived in Turkey ahead of the move and has been pictured by the club wearing the team's colours ahead of signing his contract on Thursday.

Salah is just two seasons removed from an outstanding Premier League campaign where he scored 29 goals and made 18 assists in 2024-25, so to see the 34-year-old end up in the Super Lig is somewhat surprising.

Bordo-Mavili formasıyla ilk kez kameraların karşısında… İlk mesajı Büyük Trabzonspor Taraftarına:

“Bize Her Yer Trabzon!” ❤️💙#SalahIsComing pic.twitter.com/Sr1KcRDwpk

But the forward scored just seven league goals in his final season at Liverpool, with his minutes diminished amid a falling out with former Reds boss Arne Slot, so it also makes sense that Salah's range of suitors was somewhat limited.

Still, the assumption was that Salah would have the pick of clubs from the Saudi Pro League or the MLS, or even an illustrious European side who could offer him the chance for a final campaign in the Champions League.

Trabzonspor, by contrast, are generally viewed as the fourth-biggest side in Turkey, behind Istanbul giants Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, and Besiktas.

Based in the city of Trabzon, on the Black Sea, Trabzonspor have been champions of Turkey seven times, with their most recent title coming in 2021-22.

Managed by former Turkey international Fatih Tekke, Trabzonspor finished third in Super Lig last season - behind champions Galatasaray and runners-up Fenerbahce.

They are yet to qualify for the Europa League league phase, and face a two-legged play-off this month – so European football is by no means a guarantee.

Should Salah sign for Trabzonspor, the Egypt captain would instantly become the club's biggest signing. Former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pepe are among their former players.

Their current squad includes on-loan Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, as well as a couple of Cape Verde's World Cup stars: Wagner Pina and Sidny Lopes Cabral, who scored their stunning goal against Argentina.

As Salah is a free transfer, Trabzonspor would have been able to commit more of their transfer budget towards Salah's wages. His last contract at Liverpool was enormous and reported to be worth £400,000 per week.

As one of the sport's biggest global stars, Salah offers huge upside to Trabzonspor and their sponsors commercially. Trabzonspor's main shirt sponsor, financial services company Papapa, also holds naming rights for their stadium.

Salah has been pictured wearing Trabzonspor's colours and is set to arrive in the city on Wednesday before signing his contract. "Trabzon, are you ready? See you very soon," he said.

title: Here's five UConn football storylines heading into fall camp
description: UConn football enters fall camp with new coach, overhauled roster and QB battle. Here's five storylines to keep an eye on.
fullText:
UConn football enters a new era at full speed.

Jason Candle, the architect of the winningest decade in Toledo history, will take the practice field on Wednesday, Aug. 5 aiming to keep the program's momentum intact.

The Huskies are coming off back-to-back nine-win seasons under former coach Jim Mora, who left to become the head coach at Colorado State.

Candle arrives in Storrs with a track record built on consistency. Candle, who presided over the Toledo program for 10 seasons, won two Mid-American Conference championships, made seven trips to bowl games and left the Ohio program without a losing season in his tenure.

Candle isn't interested in a rebuild. But he does realize a foundation for the program must be established in Year 1.

"I think it's critical," Candle said on media day when asked how important it is to continue UConn's recent success. "I think we have to define what's realistic terms for for this team. Yesterday's home runs don't win today's game. Our successes or this program's successes or failures, either way, have no impact on what is going to go on here when this ball gets kicked off in September here. ?

Here are five storylines to watch out for as Fall camp begins on Wednesday.

Candle spent 10 seasons building Toledo into one of the most dependable programs in the Group of Five — two MAC titles, seven bowl trips and a decade without a single losing season.

He also proved he could identify and develop talent, sending 34 players to the NFL, including first-round cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and longtime Kansas City Chiefs contributor Kareem Hunt.

Now UConn is betting that formula holds up at a higher level, handing Candle a six-year deal to build on the momentum Jim Mora left behind after consecutive 9-3 seasons.

UConn's roster is almost entirely different from last season, having brought in 64 new additions to Storrs.

Candle went deep into the transfer portal, bringing 57 players in the spring. He also added seven incoming freshmen.

The offense has been completely overhauled as big-name transfers such as running back Cyncir Bowers, wide receiver Ryder Treadway and offensive lineman Dominic Rivera will look to make instant impacts.

On defense, the Huskies added former Michigan State defensive lineman Avery Dunn, Toledo standout Esean Carter, linebacker Zakaih Saez and defensive back Jayden Davis.

Among the slew of transfers, Candle brought over 22 players from Toledo.

UConn's quarterback competition is shaping up to be the most closely watched storyline of fall camp. Four players are in the mix, and Candle isn't ready to commit to any of them.

Kalieb Osborne enters as the presumptive favorite after spending two years learning Candle's offense at Toledo. He flashed his dual-threat ability in the Boca Raton Bowl, throwing for a touchdown and adding 77 rushing yards.

But he's not running away with the job.

Redshirt freshman Jake Merklinger, a former four-star recruit who spent two seasons at Tennessee without ever cracking the starting lineup, brings the kind of arm talent and size that make him a threat to leapfrog the more experienced options.

Behind them, redshirt junior Tucker McDonald offers steadiness and experience from three appearances a season ago, while true freshman Bo Polston — a Candle recruit who followed him from his Toledo commitment — is working his way back from a shoulder injury that cost him his final high school season.

Offensive coordinator Nunzio Campanile has made clear the staff won't rush a decision just to have one, which means this battle could stretch deep into camp.

Candle is known to be an offensive-forward coach, but his fingerprints are all over this UConn defense.

New defensive coordinator Ryan Manalac, who was previously a linebackers coach at Pitt, will have plenty to work with as Candle brought over all-conference linebacker K'Von Sherman. Sherman led Toledo in tackles last season with 93 and is expected to anchor the front seven.

UConn also brought in former Penn defensive tackle John Lista, who earned unanimous all-Ivy League honors last season after finishing the year with 78 tackles and two sacks.

The secondary has more questions, but Candle's track record suggests he can get the most out of young defensive backs. Look for players like Jayden Davis, Tyler McKinstry and Moussa Kane to be contenders to have breakout years.

Despite having a first-year coach, an almost entirely new roster and no conference to call home, the Huskies have a schedule that would favor them getting to their fourth bowl game in five years.

UConn has seven home games, starting with the Huskies' season opener against Lafayette on Sept. 5.

UConn should be favored against Lafayette, Southern Mississippi, Temple, UMass and Old Dominion. The Huskies will have tougher matchups against Maryland, Syracuse, North Carolina and James Madison; however all of those games will be at home.

title: Nick Wright brutally explains why LA Lakers are the biggest losers in LeBron James’ free agency saga
description: The Los Angeles Lakers are being called the clear losers in LeBron James’ free agency saga this offseason. Following an eight-season run, LeBron James and the Los Angeles Lakers went their separate ways this offseason.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers are being called the clear losers in LeBron James' free agency saga this offseason.

Following an eight-season run, LeBron James and the Los Angeles Lakers went their separate ways this offseason.

What followed was a few weeks of massive rumors, but James ultimately joined the Philadelphia 76ers to boost his chances of winning a fifth NBA Championship of his career.

With the dust settled, NBA analyst Nick Wright assessed the entire saga and came up with a clear loser from it.

When James joined the Lakers in 2018, the organization was in a rebuilding phase post the Kobe Bryant era. As a result, every major NBA star was hesitant to join the Purple and Gold. However, James decided to risk it all and signed with the Lakers.

Speaking of James' split with the Lakers, the analyst reminded the franchise of the 4x NBA champion's decision and how they should be forever indebted to him.

"Far and away, the biggest loser of this whole thing is the Lakers. LeBron James saved the d___ franchise.

"That team telling everyone who would listen what a pain in the a__ LeBron is led to a scenario where LeBron James was willing to play for the league minimum, but not for them," Wright said.

"Every single move that the Lakers made this offseason… you could have done all of that and still brought LeBron back. Instead, they couldn't wait for the LeBron James era to be over," Wright added.

Considering that James is still an All-NBA caliber player and signed a veteran's minimum deal with the 76ers shows that he was willing to take a massive pay cut.

Unfortunately, the Lakers weren't willing to do that for James in favor of Luka Doncic taking over the team asap. Fans will find out which side made the correct decision after the conclusion of the 2026-27 NBA season.
