fullText:
Following their successful 2025-26 season that saw them advance to the Eastern Conference Final, the Montreal Canadiens and general manager Kent Hughes re-signed both Ivan Demidov and Jakub Dobes to multi-year contracts.

The good news for the Canadiens is that they appear set up to be a force in the Atlantic Division for a long time with so many of their core pieces locked up for the foreseeable future under contract. However, one player that still is in need of a few deal before next season is hard-nosed defenseman Arber Xhekaj.

Currently, he's a restricted free agent following the expiration of his most recent contract that carried a salary cap hit of $1.3 million.

According to Herb Zurkowsky of The Montreal Gazette, the Calgary Flames showed interest in Xhekaj at last season's NHL Trade Deadline.

"Another source revealed Calgary's interest in Xhekaj last season at the trade deadline," he wrote.

According to NHL Insider David Pagnotta, there isn't much to report in terms of movement on a new deal between the Canadiens and Xhekaj.

"At the time we're doing this right now, the update is status quo conversationally between the Habs and Xekaj," he said. "They're not the only one to want to have that sandpaper in the lineup, there are other teams that have expressed over the last few weeks interest in trading for Arber Xhekaj, but the Canadiens have valued him for some time and they haven't pulled the trigger. A, they haven't found a deal they want because B, they want to keep the player. You've gotta convince them to make it happen."

Pagnotta then revealed that one of the clubs that showed interest in Xhekaj was the Philadelphia Flyers, a club that always welcomes grit and sandpaper in their lineup.

"The very quick update with respect to Xhekaj and the Canadiens, despite interest from other teams – I mean, Philadelphia is one, and they've had interest in him during the last couple of years and is still the case now – but nothing done on that front yet," he said. "And contractually, status quo. They'll go back and forth to try and bridge whatever gap there is; both sides being very quiet on that side."

Pagnotta's words of there not being any rush to get a deal done for Xhekaj were recently confirmed by his agent Brian Bartlett, who noted that there is still plenty of time between now and the start of next season.

"We have a long time until the season starts," Bartlett said. "We have to try and figure out where he fits into the structure of the team. Montreal has some decisions to make. We have some decisions to make. There's no panic."

"I think he's a really good player," he continued. "Good teams like good players. The communication has been positive with the management group. I don't have any indication to think that things are going to go off the rail."

title: Atlanta Braves Release Andrew McCutchen From Minor League Contract
description: The Braves released McCutchen, who did not appear with the big league team after being signed to a minor-league contract in early July.
fullText:
The Braves released the veteran outfielder after a month in their organization.

The Atlanta Braves announced they have released outfielder Andrew McCutchen from his minor league contract.

McCutchen had signed a minor league deal with the team last month and had been playing with Triple-A Gwinnett, with hopes of working his way back up to the major leagues.

The transaction was McCutchen exercising an opt-out clause in his contract with Atlanta, per Stephen J. Nesbitt of The Athletic. He most likely wants a better path to the big leagues instead of cracking his way into the Braves' outfield.

With the recent addition of right-handed outfielder Lane Thomas to the Braves' roster, whom they acquired from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline, Atlanta essentially fulfilled their need for a right-handed bat at the position, while not opting to select McCutchen. He did not play a game for the Braves' big league team this season.

McCutchen, now 39, signed his minor league contract with the Braves on July 2, a little over a month after he had been released by the Texas Rangers in late May. He had played in parts of 37 games with the Rangers this season, posting a .192 batting average in 73 at-bats.

In what turned out to be a very short stint with Triple-A Gwinnett, McCutchen had himself a solid stretch in just 30 at-bats. In nine games, he hit .333 at the plate and recorded 10 hits.

The former NL MVP with the Pittsburgh Pirates had broken camp with the Rangers and made their Opening Day roster. Now well beyond his prime, his bat has primarily been utilized as a platoon against left-handed pitching, his strong suit at the plate.

McCutchen had made his return to Pittsburgh in 2023 after playing for four separate teams in between his initial stint with the team, and performed at a very productive level. From 2023-2025, even in the later years of his career, he impressed as a league-average bat and a lefty specialist.

Atlanta's release of McCutchen was not the only release of a veteran in their organization. Left-handed pitcher Austin Gomber and outfielder Ben Gamel were also released from their Triple-A affiliate.

McCutchen still may factor into the mix of a team's outfield, though doing so for a contender may be unlikely for the right-handed bat now in the back half of his career. After the deadline, the Braves now add Thomas to an outfield that consists of Ronald Acuña Jr, Michael Harris and Mike Yastrzemski.

title: Jesse Minter’s clear standard is accelerating the Ravens' transition
description: Mike Mickens credits Jesse Minter with creating a clear standard that keeps Baltimore’s defensive coaches and players aligned.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens assembled their new defensive staff from different levels of football and several coaching backgrounds. Jesse Minter's first challenge was ensuring all of those voices delivered one message. Mike Mickens believes the new head coach has accomplished that through a clearly defined standard.

"He has us on the same page, and he has a clear message," Mickens said on The Ravens Lounge. "We want to be the best in everything that we do."

Mickens arrived from Notre Dame to become Baltimore's defensive pass game coordinator and secondary coach. Anthony Weaver returned as defensive coordinator, while other assistants carried experience from different NFL and college systems. Those perspectives can strengthen a staff, but they can also create confusion if position coaches use conflicting terminology or teach different responses to the same situation. Minter's leadership is intended to remove that gray area. Players should hear the same philosophy regardless of which coach leads the meeting or corrects a practice rep.

The approach is particularly important in the secondary. Defensive backs must communicate coverage checks, route distribution and motions within seconds. A hesitation by one player can turn a routine adjustment into an explosive completion. Mickens said the staff has clearly explained its processes and expectations from the top down. That consistency allows assistants to focus on technique without creating questions about the defense's larger objective.

Baltimore is also working through a significant transition after an 8-9 season led to the departure of longtime coach John Harbaugh. Players are learning Minter's system while adjusting to new teachers and practice expectations. A complicated defensive playbook becomes manageable when the coaching points remain consistent. Minter's task is to make sure the same language connects the meeting room, practice field, and game-day headset.

The Ravens will ultimately judge the system by points allowed, takeaways and victories. Before those results arrive, Minter is establishing the shared understanding required to produce them.

According to Mickens, every defensive coach already knows the standard he is expected to reinforce.

title: Blue Jays pitcher suddenly leaves game while warming up
description: The right-hander only pitched two innings against the Astros
fullText:
Trey Yesavage's latest start ended earlier than expected.

The Toronto Blue Jays' right-hander was forced to come out of his start against the Houston Astros on Aug. 4 while experiencing "some kind of discomfort while warming up," according to Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet.

Reliever Chad Dallas replaced Yesavage in the bottom of the third inning at Daikin Park in Houston.

MORE: Father of Blue Jays pitcher dies while visiting family on team's road trip

Yesavage faced seven batters across two scoreless innings to begin the game, allowing one walk and no hits. The game was still tied 0-0 after the top of the third inning when Yesavage walked off the mound with Blue Jays manager John Schneider and a trainer after throwing a few practice pitches.

The cause of the injury is unclear. Whatever ailed him, it did not appear to affect Yesavage's right arm. He tapped his left (landing) foot a couple times before he was visited by Schneider and the trainer. He stepped somewhat gingerly on the foot as they walked off.

The Blue Jays have not announced why Yesavage left the game.

MORE: Wife of Dodgers veteran has harsh reaction to trade rumors

Yesavage is 5-5 with a 3.73 ERA in his first full MLB season.

After winning the American League pennant a year ago, the Blue Jays got off to a 53-60 start 2026, all but mathematically eliminating them from contention. They traded pitcher Kevin Gausman to the Chicago Cubs ahead of the trade deadline on Monday, Aug. 3.

Toronto also acquired pitcher Jose Soriano from the Los Angeles Angels to replace Gausman. Now they might need to find a substitute for Yesavage, who has been their second-best starter behind Dylan Cease.

MORE: Blue Jays make trade with Angels that no one saw coming

Dallas, a 26-year-old rookie, had been starting at Triple-A. He could be the next man up if the Jays continue to roll a six-man rotation.

Toronto also acquired veteran right-hander Jameson Taillon, who had been designated for assignment by the Cubs, in a cash trade just before the deadline.

title: Brewers send pitcher Brandon Sproat to Triple-A after acquiring Dustin May
description: With the Milwaukee Brewers’ trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.  Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.  May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — With the Milwaukee Brewers' trade-deadline acquisition of veteran starter Dustin May, rookie right-hander Brandon Sproat became the odd man out of the rotation.

Sproat, who appeared in 21 games for Milwaukee, including 19 starts, was optioned Tuesday to Triple-A Nashville one day after another inconsistent start.

May, acquired from the Cardinals on Monday along with reliever JoJo Romero, is scheduled to start Thursday for Milwaukee in the series finale against Pittsburgh. Left-hander Kyle Harrison, on the injured list since July 9, also is scheduled to return and start Wednesday.

The 25-year-old Sproat, acquired from the Mets in the offseason trade for Freddy Peralta, is 3-7 with a 5.27 ERA for Milwaukee. He has not won in five starts since his last victory on June 30.

"I think you look at it at face value. It wasn't a foregone conclusion," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said before Tuesday's game. "It's really about what's best for the player and what's best for the team."

Sproat took the loss Monday in a 4-3 defeat in the series opener against the Pirates, allowing four runs on five hits in three-plus innings. He was removed after throwing consecutive wild pitches following a leadoff single in the fourth.

Sproat has struck out 100 in 95 2/3 innings with the Brewers. But he walked 48, hit nine batters and threw nine wild pitches.

"The free bases, the wild pitches, the walks, hit by pitches, has got to stop," Murphy said. "You can't pitch in the big leagues like that."

May was 5-7 with a 4.38 ERA in 21 starts with St. Louis, including 0-1 with a 4.62 ERA in six July starts.

The Brewers also optioned reliever Garrett Stallings to Nashville on Tuesday. In addition to getting Romero, Milwaukee also acquired reliever Antonio Senzatela from Colorado on Monday.

title: Terry McLaurin Issues Clear Message Amid Commanders’ WR Concerns
description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin is trying to be a calming influence as the team deals with major questions at his position. The post Terry McLaurin Issues Clear Message Amid Commanders’ WR Concerns appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders have several questions at wide receiver with the second week of training camp now in full swing, but Terry McLaurin assured the team and its fans that they need not worry about the position group — at least not at the very top.

McLaurin held out for a new contract last offseason following a Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro campaign. He ultimately landed a three-year contract worth $97 million, but stumbled in 2025 due to the first meaningful injury concerns of his career (quad strain and ankle sprain).

For the first time since his rookie year in 2019, McLaurin failed to eclipse 1,000 receiving yards. Quarterback Jayden Daniels also battled injuries all season long and played in just seven contests. The result was a 5-12 record, the exact inverse of the 12-5 campaign that Daniels and McLaurin helped muster in 2024, which ended with the team in the NFC Championship Game.

But on Monday, August 3, McLaurin told Jeremy Fowler of ESPN that he is at full strength again just six weeks out from the new season and is keyed up for what is to come.

"My body feels great," Mclaurin said. "I'm clocking 22 mph, not missing any days. So I just feel like my normal self. And when you're out here from Day 1 all the way through camp, obviously you get in that full conditioning mode. … This has been my home for going on eight years now, and I'm super excited just to be here for the whole entire season."

GettyWashington Commanders rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams.

McLaurin back at full strength, alongside Daniels also at 100 percent, is a huge boon for the Commanders offense. That said, there are still multiple WR slots waiting for someone to step up and fill them.

ESPN's John Keim wrote Monday that the wideout position battle is the most compelling on Washington's roster this summer on multiple levels.

"Washington probably will mix and match depending on the matchups and the game plan, but players still have to earn time — whether it's third-round pick Antonio Williams or past draft choices Jaylin Lane and Luke McCaffrey," Keim wrote. "The Commanders also have veterans Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Van Jefferson. So the battle is not only to earn time as a No. 2 but also potentially just for a roster spot."

GettyFree agent wide receiver Stefon Diggs.

One card the Commanders may still have to play is attempting to sign Stefon Diggs in free agency.

Diggs, who was the leading receiver on a New England Patriots team that played in the Super Bowl in February, has as much interest in Washington as the Commanders have in him.

"I'm told free agent Stefon Diggs is on the radar," Fowler reported Tuesday. "Washington is monitoring the situation with Diggs, who's intrigued by the chance to play in Washington (he's from the area). Let's see how things play out, but it seems like this is a realistic option as the sides keep in contact."

title: Browns' Shedeur Sanders Lands Brutal Take From NFL Execs
description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders has received a harsh take from NFL executives.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns have a quarterback battle heading into the 2026 season between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders.

Ahead of the season, executives and coaches ranked Sanders 35th out of 35 veteran quarterbacks.

"I'd sleep like a baby if I got to play him every week," one defensive coordinator said about Sanders.

This is harsh criticism of Sanders, who was inconsistent in his rookie season but showed flashes of potential.

"He's inaccurate at all three levels. I can't tell if he's going to get better, but there's a huge gap between him and competent QB play," one executive said about Sanders.

In the 2025 season, Sanders appeared in eight games, starting in seven, and completed 56.6 percent of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. He also rushed for 169 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries.

The 24-year-old quarterback is in a battle with former star quarterback Watson, whose tenure in Cleveland has been plagued by injuries and off-field controversies. Watson has appeared in 19 games for the Browns, completing 61.2 percent of his passes for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. He also rushed for 465 yards and three touchdowns on the ground.

The 30-year-old quarterback is entering the final year of his contract with Cleveland, and they hope he can return to the player he was when he was with the Houston Texans.

Watson's last dynamic season came in 2020, when he was one of the best quarterbacks in the league, completing 70.2 percent of his passes for 4,823 yards, 33 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. He also rushed for 444 yards and three touchdowns on 90 carries.

While he was once a star quarterback, Watson has never played at that level for the Browns, failing to live up to the five-year, $250 million guaranteed contract they gave him after acquiring him from the Texans.

The quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson will be pivotal for Cleveland to have a successful season, as they will need one of them to emerge as a quality player to win games in 2026.

title: Next MLS Commissioner Berg Is Ready To Ride The FIFA World Cup Wave
description: Larry Berg, the next MLS commissioner, doesn't plan on sitting on his hands or the league's laurels, realizing the it needs to use the recent World Cup to grow even more.
fullText:
When he was eight years old while growing up in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, the father of Larry Berg saw a poster on a telephone pole about a new youth soccer league starting up.

"We basically had two teams," Larry said. "We played each other every weekend, and it grew from there. I fell in love with the game, and I learned about World Cups. I learned about the broader universe, and I became a student of the game. I became a fan of all the leagues that have been in the U.S. I certainly became a fan of the U.S. men's national team and ultimately a fan of Major League Soccer."

Today, he is more than a fan of MLS. He is the commissioner of the 30-team league.

Berg, 60, was introduced to the media at league headquarters in Midtown Manhattan on Tuesday as the successor to Don Garber, who will step down as commissioner after 27 years at the helm at the end of the year. He will become the third commissioner in league history. Doug Logan was the first, from 1996-99.

Berg, who will divest his interest as co-owner of the Los Angeles Football Club, will be concerned with more than just one team. He has been charged with leading MLS in riding the wave that the 2026 FIFA World Cup created.

"The foundation has been built," he said. "Now it's our responsibility to build on it, and that's what excites me most.

"I didn't accept this role to protect what we've already accomplished. I accepted it because I believe this league is ready for its next chapter. I believe Major League Soccer has entered a new era. The foundation is strong. The opportunity is extraordinary, and I have complete confidence that working together will seize it."

MLS must seize the opportunity for growth on the short and long term. The 1994 World Cup gave birth to the league. The 2026 World Cup can be a catalyst to boost it to an even higher orbit.

"The World Cup this summer reminded all of us why this sport captures the imagination of billions of people around the world. Millions of people across North America experienced that passion firsthand," Berg said. "They fell in love with the drama, the atmosphere, the supporter culture and the emotion that makes soccer unlike anything else.

"For many, it was also their first meaningful introduction to the global game, and that creates an extraordinary opportunity for all of us. The question isn't whether people are paying attention to soccer - they are. The question is what we do with this moment.

"Our responsibility now is to make sure the people discovering our league today become supporters for life. That means strengthening the connection between our clubs and their communities, creating unforgettable experiences for fans, and making sure the excitement generated this summer becomes lasting momentum for Major League Soccer."

While many teams boast capacity crowds, MLS needs to boost its streaming ratings.

When its 10-year, $2.3 billion deal with Apple TV was announced in 2023, fans needed an MLS Season Pass subscription to view matches. In 2025, the deal was cut to 2029.

When the deal winds up in 2029, the league will have to decide whether to renew with Apple or pursue other opportunities.

The deal ends in 2029, leaving MLS to decide whether to renew with Apple or pursue other partners.

Berg said that the next deal will be "finding media partners that want to co-create the future with us."

MLS is one of the few leagues in the world that doesn't include promotion or relegation. And during Berg's reign, he doesn't expect that to change.

"I can understand the appeal for the fan, [but] I don't think it's a great way to build a league," Berg said. "I don't think it's a way to get stadiums built and to get training facilities built and to have owners invest in rosters and all the other things you need to do. So I don't think it's appropriate for our league.

"I think Don has said before, never say never, but I just don't see it happening anytime soon."

During Garber's tenure, the league grew from 12 to 30 franchises. He helped concoct a plan to save the league from extinction when it dropped from 2 to 10 teams in 2001. Salaries rose appreciably. MLS attracted such top-notch players such as David Beckham and Lionel Messi. The former is still playing for Inter Miami CF.

Garber, who will become MLS chairman in 2027, had little doubt that the board of governors selected the right man to succeed him.

"In Larry, our league has found exactly the leader that we need at this time because, most importantly, Larry loves the game," he said. "He understands it because he helped build it. He knows our clubs and knows our league because he's experienced it full-time and understands the opportunities and the challenges ahead. He really understands that our best days are ahead.

"I will say that leading MLS is going to be one of the great privileges of your life, Larry. I think your integrity, your ambition, your thoughtfulness, your smarts, and your respect that you have for the game is going to help take this league to where we all want it to go."

Michael Lewis, the sixth recipient of the Clay Berling Media Career of Excellence Award in 2025, can be followed on X an Bluesky at @Soccerwriter. His 10th soccer book, Around the World Cup in 40 Years: An American sportswriter's perspective, has been published.

title: Buccaneers, Baker Mayfield Contract Dispute May Have Unexpected Outcome: Insider
description: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have plans for Baker Mayfield in 2027. That does not necessarily mean that they have plans for him to be on the team, though. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN was at Bucs training camp and got an inside scoop on what the team might be thinking.He came away feeling that the two […] The post Buccaneers, Baker Mayfield Contract Dispute May Have Unexpected Outcome: Insider appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have plans for Baker Mayfield in 2027. That does not necessarily mean that they have plans for him to be on the team, though. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN was at Bucs training camp and got an inside scoop on what the team might be thinking.

He came away feeling that the two sides are on a "collision course" for a franchise tag that would cost at least $47 million. However, Fowler believes a tag-and-trade could be the unexpected end result of this contract dispute.

"The tag could also be a way for the Bucs to facilitate a trade to a QB-needy team, acquiring draft capital to select the quarterback of the future," wrote Fowler on August 4. "The Bucs have always expressed complete faith in Mayfield, but this would at least be an option."

Fowler went on to note that because Mayfield has always had success with coaches from the Sean McVay or Kyle Shanahan coaching tree, a trade to a team that has one of those styles of coaches would make sense. Fowler even threw out the Los Angeles Rams as a destination for Mayfield to return to next season if Matthew Stafford retired.

The Rams just drafted Ty Simpson, but the Bucs would want something significant back for Mayfield if they decided to give him the franchise tag. That would likely mean he earned a noteworthy deal.

So, there is a scenario where the Rams do not have to give up much in draft capital, because Simpson is part of the deal. From the Bucs' perspective, they would be in a tough spot losing Mayfield if he played well next year.

They would likely not be picking high enough to make a move in the draft, and they would not have the money to tie him up. So, they could still move on from Mayfield while also finding his replacement. Simpson would come with a team-friendly deal for the next couple of seasons, so the team could get out of the high-money quarterback business as well.

Mayfield noted that he did not think the Bucs could franchise tag him after the season because of their cap structure. However, the leak to Fowler shows just the opposite and opens a door that Mayfield did not consider when he talked to the media.

So, the Bucs likely still feel good about not extending Mayfield. If he plays well, they can tag him and keep him, tag him and trade him, or tag him and then work on an extension. However, if he does not play well, the team will be happy that they did not engage in a long-term extension with him.

He started hot for them last year, and they were 6-3. However, they finished 2-6, in part because his play dropped off. The Bucs do not want to be stuck with that if it happens again.

So, while it is disappointing for Mayfield, it is hard to knock the Bucs for their plan. The two sides will have to wait to see how Mayfield plays before anything else can happen.

title: Venus Williams Takes New Role With Gatorade’s Body of Science
description: Venus Williams becomes the first ambassador for Gatorade’s Body of Science, supporting research built around women’s unique needs.
fullText:
Venus Williams Takes New Role With Gatorade's Body of Science appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Venus Williams has spent her career setting standards in competition, business and culture. Her newest role asks her to help change the science available to women.

Gatorade selected Williams as the inaugural ambassador for "Body of Science," its multi-year international research commitment focused on women's nutrition and hydration, Pepsico reports. The program will operate through GSSI, the company's human-performance research division.

Williams will promote the initiative and draw attention to a striking imbalance. Information released with the program says only 6% of sports science research worldwide examines women exclusively. For years, researchers have frequently treated findings about male physiology as broadly applicable, leaving women with fewer answers tailored to their bodies.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Williams framed her involvement as an investment in women beyond her own era.

"This work is so important because it's not just about me, it's about the women who come after me," Williams said.

She also noted that women have tested their physical limits while relying on studies originally built around men. What energizes her, she explained, is Gatorade's willingness to investigate specific questions and produce knowledge women have lacked.

The partnership carries more than celebrity value. Williams brings the perspective of a tennis champion, entrepreneur, author and style figure to a program designed to reach beyond athletic competition.

GSSI will explore women's needs during key experiences and life phases, including pregnancy, perimenopause and menstruation. Early research has already involved 500 participants.

Williams' task will involve making that work visible as GSSI develops and publishes peer-reviewed studies. Gatorade did not simply hire a recognizable spokesperson. It chose someone whose career reflects the program's larger point: women deserve research that starts with their bodies, experiences and questions.

title: Cowboys suffer first season-ending injury, TE out for year with ACL
description: The Cowboys suffered their first casualty of camp as tight end Princeton Fant suffered a torn ACL on the first day of padded practice.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys first padded practice came at a cost as reserve tight end Princeton Fant has suffered a season-ending knee injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed an initially feared diagnosis that the fourth-year tight end tore his ACL and partially tore his MCL.

He will have surgery at a later date, but the fourth-year veteran's road ahead is now centered on an extensive rehabilitation process and recovery, putting his immediate future on hold.

Per Brian Schottenheimer, TE Princeton Fant suffered an ACL, partial MCL injury. He'll undergo surgery in a few weeks. #dallascowboys

Initial reports confirmed Fant would undergo further testing, including an MRI, to determine the severity of the injury.

Fant was engaged in a blocking rep on a running play against edge Sam Williams when he suffered the injury, immediately falling onto the ground. He remained down for several moments before being helped to the sideline and eventually carted off, unable to put weight on his left leg.

Princeton Fant left on a cart after this collision: pic.twitter.com/f5ZkkFTWyn

Fant entered the league as a 2023 undrafted free agent out of Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons in Dallas working towards a permanent roster spot. He had appeared in 11 career games but has yet to catch a regular season pass.

Dallas maintains depth at tight end with Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford headlining. Fant was in competition with Luke Schoonmaker along with UDFAs Michael Trigg and DJ Rogers. Fant's absence thins the unit's overall versatility.

Repetitions that would have gone to Fant will now have to be redistributed, potentially accelerating the developmental timeline for others. Fant will move to the IR list, opening up a roster spot for a new addition who will try and make his mark and impress the coaching staff.

title: Vikings legend critical of some of J.J. McCarthy's decision-making
description: Adrian Peterson spoek recently about the Vikings quarterback battle and that included some thoughts on J.J. McCarthy's play.
fullText:
The Minnesota Vikings quarterback competition is heating up now that training camp is here, and no one is backing down on social media from defending who they think should win the job. Through it all, the coaching staff has remained steadfast in their execution of this quarterback competition, while some on the outside consider it already Kyler Murray's job to lose.

While no starter is close to being named, it does allow time for more folks to add their thoughts. The latest comments come from franchise legend Adrian Peterson. He spoke recently with Kyle Odegard of Rotogrinders and shed some light on his thoughts on one half of the battle.

title: Vikings Training Camp Notes: 8/4 Edition
description: The Vikings held another training camp practice today, this one in shells. Overall it was a lighter practice- tomorrow’s practice is to be a longer, padded practice, so not as many things to report from this practice, but certainly some tidbids here and there. On the Quarterback Competition Other Notes That’s all I have for […]
fullText:
The Vikings held another training camp practice today, this one in shells. Overall it was a lighter practice- tomorrow's practice is to be a longer, padded practice, so not as many things to report from this practice, but certainly some tidbids here and there.

It was a decent day for both quarterbacks generally. Both had some mildly good throws between team and redzone drills and some inaccurate ones. Probably more par for the course rather than terribly concerning. No deep bombs again today. Mostly short stuff with some intermediate throws mixed in for both QBs.

There was a lot of mixing and matching between 1s and 2s and even 3s today on both sides of the ball.

Some of the team drills today looked more like a half-speed install. The offense was working against staff members while the defense was doing the same on the other field.

However, it was noteworthy that in the last portion of full-speed team drills that Kyler Murray was exclusively with the first-team and J.J. McCarthy was exclusively with the second-team. Perhaps a sign of things to come.

I said it yesterday and I'll say it again today: Charles Demmings looks like the real deal. He had multiple PBUs again today and plays with swagger. So far, he looks like the best draft pick of the bunch. He can be physical, and he may have to tone that down to some degree to avoid penalties, but he plays with confidence no matter which receiver he is up against- and its often either Jefferson, Addison, or Felton. He looked to be getting regular reps with the first-team defense today.

Christian Darrisaw did not practice today, nor did Andrew Van Ginkel and I believe Blake Cashman. It was kind of a veteran's day off today between two padded practices.

Domonique Orange was in uniform today, but I didn't see him participating in team drills. Still, probably a positive sign that he should return sooner rather than later.

Demond Claiborne participated in team drills as well, although he had a drop in red zone drills.

I watched most of the offensive line drills today and I don't think there will be a serious challenge to either Blake Brandel or Michael Jurgens at center. Vershon Lee is more cross-training at center but still primarily a guard. I don't see either Gavin Gerhardt or Walter Rouse making the team at this point, although they have a shot to change that- but probably not a big one. They are last in the pecking order and I'm not sure Rouse will have much of an opportunity to compete at guard. He's not going to win a roster spot at tackle with Ryan Van Demark and Caleb Tiernan basically roster locks.

Jauan Jennings is not a dynamic athlete compared to the other receivers on the roster. He has value as a blocker and can win contested catches with his size and physicality, but he's not likely to create much separation as a route runner.

Tai Felton could earn some reps this year on offense as a more dynamic third wide receiver.

Caleb Banks had a few snaps with the first team, but that was it. That was the case yesterday too. They are slowly working him in and hopefully will begin to increase his snap count.

Jake Golday had a couple nice plays in run defense- disrupting runs in the backfield

Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins continues to work with the first-team and had a nice TFL on a run play.

The third-string defensive tackles got more snaps today- this was a practice where backups got more reps generally- including Eric Johnson and Taki Taimani.

TE Gavin Bartholomew continues to have a good training camp. He looks like he could end up as TE3.

That's all I have for today. I'll be back tomorrow.

title: David Mirkovic injury update: Illinois star undergoes foot surgery, return undetermined
description: Illinois star David Mirkovic underwent surgery after suffering a foot injury in practice on July 31, the program announced Aug. 4.
fullText:
Illinois forward David Mirkovic, one of the best true freshmen in men's college basketball last season, is out indefinitely after undergoing surgery on his left foot, the program announced Tuesday, Aug. 4.

Mirkovic is expected to make a full recovery, according to the announcement. The injury occurred during a team practice on July 31.

Mirkovic averaged 13.3 points with eight rebounds and 2.6 rebounds per game last season, and was expected to take on an even bigger role in 2026-27 following leading scorer Keaton Wagler's departure to the NBA. Illinois didn't release a timetable for the potential All-American's return.

The Niksic, Montenegro, native helped lead Illinois to the Final Four last season, scoring a career-high 29 points in Illinois' first-round NCAA Tournament win over Penn. He also scored 14 points with 10 rebounds in the Fighting Illini's Sweet 16 win over Houston.

Illinois returns star guard Andrej Stojakovic and standout center Tomislav Ivisic, while adding highly sought-after guard Stefan Vaaks from Providence in the transfer portal. The Fighting Illini don't have an obvious forward replacement for Mirkovic, but could potentially move to a double-big lineup with Zvonomir Ivisic, Tomislav Ivisic's brother.

title: Fix this common flaw to stabilize the clubface and improve contact
description: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero shares how you can keep from stalling near contact and hit more crisp iron shots.
fullText:
I, along with my good friend and fellow GOLF Top 100 Teacher Wayne Flint, have been working with Buddy Hansen, one of the better amateurs in the Philadelphia area, on a swing fault we see at every level of the game. As Buddy approached impact, his chest would stall. When that happens, the hands and arms have to take over the release. This is no good because any release pattern that relies on hand timing instead of proper body sequencing is going to be less reliable and predictable.

For Buddy, it showed up most in his iron play. He simply wasn't striking the ball as solidly as he wanted. He could hit a great shot, but the misses were inconsistent. His swing didn't need a rebuild, it just needed a tune-up in one specific area.

You don't have to spin your chest at top speed to play great golf, but it does need to keep moving (instead of stalling) through the downswing. We addressed it with a series of feels and drills designed to keep his pivot moving. You can see the entire progression in the latest episode of our Pro Work series below.

To start, we had Buddy allow his head to drift slightly to the right as he turned back, making it easier for his chest to complete its turn. Think of it like winding a spring. The more fully you load the spring in the backswing, the more energy you can release on the way down.

Players who stall through impact also tend to lose their posture, with the hips moving closer to the golf ball. That pushes the swing direction out to the right, and the club approaches impact on a much steeper, more upright plane. From a ground-pressure standpoint, it often feels as though pressure moves out toward the toes of the lead foot — if it ever fully gets to the lead side at all.

Instead of standing up to create space, we wanted Buddy to keep turning his chest. One feel that really helped was paying attention to where the pressure finished in his lead foot. Rather than moving toward the toes, it needed to feel as though it was settling into the heel, a good indication that his body was continuing to rotate around instead of standing up.

Once you understand that sensation, try this drill. Have a friend stand facing you a safe distance away and hold a club shaft straight out at about elbow height while taking a couple of steps toward the target side. As you swing, it should feel as though the club travels around and underneath the guide shaft. If your chest stalls and you lose your posture, you'll immediately feel as though the club wants to move upward into the shaft. (Just make sure your friend is standing far enough away that even a poor swing can't actually hit it.)

Even highly skilled players with plenty of clubhead speed fall into this pattern because standing up out of posture creates the sensation of having more room to swing the arms faster. It's one of golf's classic illusions: what feels more powerful is often less efficient. Keeping the chest turning through impact improves contact, stabilizes the clubface and ultimately produces more consistent ball speed.

title: Patriots Claim Former All-AAC WR After Cardinals Release
description: The New England Patriots have added another former draft pick to a wide receiver room already packed with competition.New England claimed Tejhaun Palmer off waivers from the Arizona Cardinals on Tuesday, Aug. 4, the team announced. The Patriots created the roster spot by releasing rookie tight end Jeremiah Franklin, who had signed shortly before training […] The post Patriots Claim Former All-AAC WR After Cardinals Release appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New England Patriots have added another former draft pick to a wide receiver room already packed with competition.

New England claimed Tejhaun Palmer off waivers from the Arizona Cardinals on Tuesday, Aug. 4, the team announced. The Patriots created the roster spot by releasing rookie tight end Jeremiah Franklin, who had signed shortly before training camp.

Palmer enters as a long-shot roster candidate, but the move gives New England another receiver with outside size and a history of creating explosive plays.

At 6-foot-2 and 210 pounds, he offers a profile differing from several of the smaller receivers fighting for work near the bottom of the depth chart.

GettyDENVER, COLORADO – AUGUST 25: Tejhaun Palmer #83 of the Arizona Cardinals catches a pass under coverage by Quinton Newsome #36 of the Denver Broncos in the fourth quarter during the preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 25, 2024 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images)

The Cardinals selected Palmer out of UAB with the No. 191 overall pick in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft.

He spent most of his first two professional seasons on Arizona's practice squad before receiving a late promotion to the active roster.

Palmer made his NFL debut against the Los Angeles Rams in the 2025 regular-season finale. He didn't record a reception, but Arizona used him on offense and special teams before bringing him back for another offseason.

The Cardinals waived Palmer on Aug. 3 while adding running back Evan Hull and defensive lineman Cam Horsley, via the team's transaction log.

New England submitted a successful claim one day later, giving Palmer an immediate opportunity to restart his roster bid.

His final college season helps explain the interest.

Palmer caught 47 passes for 858 yards and seven touchdowns at UAB in 2023. His 18.3 yards per reception led the American Athletic Conference, and he produced four 100-yard games while earning third-team all-conference honors, per his UAB biography.

That production followed a 2022 season in which Palmer averaged 16 yards per catch. He finished his three years at UAB with 83 receptions for 1,409 yards and nine touchdowns.

A pre-draft scouting report from NFL Draft Diamonds praised Palmer's frame, hands, ability to adjust to the football and willingness as a blocker. The report also identified separation and short-area quickness as concerns.

GettyFOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS – JUNE 09: Members of the New England Patriots look on during a minicamp at Gillette Stadium on June 09, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images)

Palmer joins a position group that the Patriots already described as one of their deepest in recent memory.

A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs are positioned to lead the group after New England's major offseason investment at the position. Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas give the Patriots three more experienced options before the competition reaches the developmental receivers.

The team's pre-camp position preview projected seven receivers as realistic contenders for five or six roster spots. Palmer arrives after practices have already begun, leaving him limited time to learn the offense and create separation in that race.

His clearest opening could come on special teams and during the preseason.

Palmer appeared in all three of Arizona's 2025 preseason games, catching three passes for 18 yards, and his lone regular-season appearance included work in the kicking game, according to his NFL game log.

The roster exchange also ends Franklin's brief stay in Foxborough.

The former Boston College tight end signed July 24 after playing 41 college games and catching 93 passes for 1,010 yards and six touchdowns.

For Palmer, the claim offers another chance to turn draft status and physical tools into a permanent role.

The top of New England's receiving corps appears settled.

But the final few weeks of camp will determine whether its newest addition can force his way into the conversation below it.

title: D-backs vs. Padres Discussion
description: Today’s Lineups PADRES DIAMONDBACKS Fernando Tatis – RF Corbin Carroll – RF Luis Rengifo – DH Geraldo Perdomo – SS Manny Machado – 3B Max Kepler – LF Ty France – 1B Ketel Marte – 2B Jackson Merrill – CF Nolan Arenado – 3B Xander Bogaerts – SS Lars Nootbaar – DH Freddy Fermin – […]
fullText:
The Arizona Diamondbacks made the following roster moves. The D-backs' 40-man roster is at 40.

Reported to the Major League roster: OF Lars Nootbaar (No. 21)

Placed on the Paternity List: C Gabriel Moreno

And right into the starting line-up goes the Noot, playing designated hitter in his Diamondbacks debut. In case you missed it, the corresponding move to make room on the 40-man roster, was the transfer of Zac Gallen to the 60-day IL – we're back to eight pitchers there. His original IL stint was retrospective to July 9, so he would be eligible to come off it about a week into September. That all depends on health, obviously – and then, whether the team things he can be of help in the final few weeks. There will likely be another quick roster move, tomorrow or Thuesday, when Moreno comes back from his childbirth watch. I'm thinking an optioning of Adrian Del Castillo seems most probable.

We're probably going to see even more of the Padres bullpen tonight. Their starter, Randy Vásquez, hasn't completed five innings or reached eighty pitches in a game since June 13. His last outing was 4.2 innings and 65 pitches against the Giants on July 30. Vásquez had a 2.68 ERA through his first nine starts, up to the middle of May. But he has found things tougher since, going 1-5 with a 6.45 ERA and FIP almost at the same level (6.37). With Eduardo Rodriguez taking the mound for Arizona, coming off eight shutout innings against the Pirates, it feels like a game the D-backs should win – guaranteeing they won't be overtaken in the standing by the Padres this series.

When we've been talking about all the players coming back from injury, one name has largely been forgotten. Blake Walston started a rehab assignment with the Reno Aces today. It has been a long road back for Blake, who last pitched in a game on September 24th, 2024, so almost two years ago. We'll need to see what he has after such a layoff. But he is a left-hander, so if he can prove his health and form, it's possible he could be a useful cog as the mid-inning southpaw in the Arizona bullpen, with Brandyn Garcia (so far) looking to have transitioned into the closer's role.

title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 25 - Moochie Norris (2005-06)
description: During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Norris wore only jersey Nos. 12 and 25 and put up 5.6 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game.
fullText:
The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history.

To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day.

With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover.

And for today's article, we will continue with the seventh of 14 who wore the No. 25, guard Moochie Norris. After ending his college career at West Florida, Norris was picked up with the 33rd overall selection of the 1996 NBA Draft by the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Washington, District of Columbia native played the first season of his pro career with the (then) Vancouver (now, Memphis) Grizzlies. He also played in another league, and for the Seattle SuperSonics before he signed with the Houston Rockets in 2000. His first stint with the team lasted until he was dealt to the New York Knicks in 2003, returning to the Rox in 2005 via trade, only to be dealt to the (then) New Orleans Hornets (now, Pelicans) in 2006.

During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Norris wore only jersey Nos. 12 and 25 and put up 5.6 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game.

title: Carlos Alcaraz Abandons Cincinnati Open Comeback, Sparks Ominous Reactions From Tennis World Ahead of US Open
description: Carlos Alcaraz’s comeback trail has suffered a major setback as the Spaniard has decided to withdraw from the Cincinnati Open, much to the dismay of the tennis community. Alcaraz, who has been sidelined since April due to a right wrist injury he sustained at the Barcelona Open, was set to make his highly anticipated return at the ATP Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati.
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz's comeback trail has suffered a major setback as the Spaniard has decided to withdraw from the Cincinnati Open, much to the dismay of the tennis community.

Alcaraz, who has been sidelined since April due to a right wrist injury he sustained at the Barcelona Open, was set to make his highly anticipated return at the ATP Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati. However, he has opted to withdraw, sparking conjecture about his US Open title defense.

After missing the ATP Masters 1000 events in Madrid and Rome, being forced to skip his title defense at the French Open, and remaining absent from Wimbledon, Alcaraz sparked immense excitement when it was revealed that he would make his return at the Cincinnati Open.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion further raised anticipation by resuming full-intensity training ahead of the tournament, which is scheduled to begin on Aug. 13.

Despite appearing to make progress in his preparations, Alcaraz has pulled out of the Cincinnati Open. In a statement, tournament director Bob Moran confirmed the Spaniard's withdrawal and extended his best wishes to the world No. 2.

"We know Carlos is doing everything he can to get back to playing tournaments as soon as possible. We wish him the best with his recovery and look forward to welcoming him back to Cincinnati in the future," Moran said.

The news of the Spaniard's withdrawal rattled the tennis community, with Boris Becker among those lamenting the "sad" development.

"Bad news for Cincinnati and Carlos A …," Becker commented.

Tennis journalists Ben Rothenberg and Scott Barclay shared grim predictions about Alcaraz's US Open title defense and the remainder of his 2026 season, while reporter José Morgado expressed his surprise at the decision.

"I would assume Alcaraz will also be out of the US Open now, just because it would seem so daunting to come back from a major injury into a best-of-five tournament when totally cold. Although if he's ready, I am sure Winston-Salem could find a wild card for him…," Rothenberg said.

"I have to say, I don't think he plays again this year at this point. 😭," Barclay wrote.

"Now that's surprising," Morgado posted.

MORE: Carlos Alcaraz Ditches Braids Days After Backlash Ahead of Cincinnati Open

It remains to be seen whether Carlos Alcaraz will deem himself ready to compete at the US Open, with his title defense on the line. The New York Major is scheduled to begin on Aug. 30, leaving the Spaniard with a little over three weeks to regain full match fitness and mount his comeback.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Mets’ 1986 reunion was a painful contrast to this brutal season in Flushing | Klapisch
description: The Mets honored the '86 championship team at Citi Field on Saturday.
fullText:
NEW YORK — I sat across from Ron Darling in the media dining room not long after the ceremony at Citi Field honoring the 1986 Mets on Saturday. Just about the whole crew was there, although I needed to check the names on the jerseys to recognize a couple of them.

It's been 40 years. Everyone is older and softer now. No matter. The nostalgia brought me right back to a more innocent time in Flushing, even if Citi Field was barely half-full.

It wasn't so much seeing Ray Knight in a wheelchair pushed by Howard Johnson. Or that Bobby Ojeda appeared to be limping. Or that Davey Johnson, Gary Carter and Buddy Harrelson, all deceased, had to be represented by family members.

It's that a reunion like this should've been a sell-out.

The fact that only 30,000 fans showed up spoke volumes about how far the Mets, who are 47-65 this season, have fallen this season. They lost another meaningless game to the Marlins, but the sense of melancholy ran deeper than that.

IT'S FREE: JOIN OUR METS COMMUNITY ON YOUTUBE!

It was what Darling said over lunch that stayed with me on the drive home.

"It's like we were doing a necrology update during the ceremony," Darling said. "Next time we have a reunion, there might be a half-dozen of us who won't be there."

Darling is right. One by one, year by year, the '86 legacy will fade. The process has already begun. Sure, folks will always talk about Mookie Wilson's ground ball trickling through Bill Buckner's legs and the miracle comeback against the Red Sox in the World Series. But fewer people will be around who actually saw it happen.

I'm one of them. Of the reporters who covered the '86 Mets, I'm the last who's still working full time. Dan Castellano (Star-Ledger), Marty Noble (Newsday) and Joe Durso (New York Times) have died. The others have retired or are writing part-time as freelancers.

I've been around long enough to watch baseball — and New York — become almost unrecognizable since 1986. That includes how talent was evaluated (no advanced analytics), how players spoke (unfiltered), how games were reported (by the tabloids), and how the sport was consumed by fans (without social media).

The entire city was on a first-name basis with the Mets. Lenny Dykstra was "Nails." Gary Carter was "Kid." Keith Hernandez was "Mex." Doc Gooden and Darryl Strawberry were … of course, you know.

Few teams in New York have had such a close relationship with their fan bases. And for good reason: The Mets were the glory boys back then, a roster full of charismatic characters who loved seeing their names in the papers.

As a reporter, you only had to keep your eyes and ears open. Something was bound to come your way. Of all the Mets from that golden era, Dykstra was the most entertaining. He was reckless, fearless, and consumed with rumors and innuendo.

But Dykstra also had a short attention span. He was honest, too, never bothering to hide his impatience with the interview process.

"Lenny, you got some time this morning?" I asked one morning.

Puffing on a cigarette, Dykstra answered, "Dude, you know I've got nothing to say."

"Lenny, people want to read about you," I replied.

"Dude, you've asked me all the questions before," Dykstra said. "I've given you all the answers. You know what I'm going to say. So go ahead and write the interview. What you say I said, I said. I trust ya, dude."

And with a friendly pat on the shoulder, Dykstra would leave me with an empty notebook.

I miss Davey Johnson, who was so sure of himself that he gave the Mets complete freedom of speech. He ripped the players in the papers. They ripped him right back.

Johnson loved the tabloids because he knew the big headlines irritated his boss, general manager Frank Cashen. The Mets took their cue from Johnson, especially Strawberry.

Today, he is a minister, sober and in control of his addictions. Forty years ago, Strawberry was volatile and unpredictable. Fans either loved him or loathed him, but they all wanted to know what he was like.

Like most star athletes, Strawberry was as self-centered then as he is humble today. But what was most fascinating was Strawberry's friendship not with Gooden, but with Darling.

Darling, who attended Yale, was the Robert Redford of the big leagues: handsome, intelligent, polite. Everyone assumed Darling was using baseball as a stepping stone to politics. Hence, outsiders tried to force themselves into Darling's personal life. They figured he was their ticket to bigger and better things — maybe even Hollywood.

Strawberry wasn't one of the hangers-on. Darling trusted him because Strawberry wasn't pretentious. He had no ulterior motives. Even today, Strawberry isn't afraid to tell it like it is.

Asked about the collapse of the 2026 Mets, Strawberry tore them to pieces.

"It takes fight to win here in New York," he said. "It can be so great in New York, but that's where the human part comes in when you're building a team. Who's going to lead? Somebody's gotta take the responsibility."

Strawberry was one of the main characters in the team-produced "Let's Go Mets Go" video. It was a four-minute production that debuted on Aug. 27 of that year. By then, the Mets had an insurmountable lead in the NL East. It was obvious they were heading straight for October.

The goofy, upbeat action featured the Mets, local fans and high-profile celebrity cameos, including Tony Bennett, Howard Stern, Robert Klein, Joe Piscopo, Dr. Joyce Brothers and Mayor Ed Koch.

The music, the hairstyles and the sheer audacity were pure 80s New York: pre-cell phones, pre-internet, pre-everything. I remember the 727s roaring overhead as they departed LaGuardia Airport. I remember the traffic jams on the Grand Central Parkway leading to Shea Stadium, especially on the nights Gooden was pitching. I remember when the Mets were more important than the Yankees.

Yankees GM Brian Cashman invokes the unthinkable with pennant race looming | KlapischAug. 4, 2026, 9:49 a.m.

Yankees' Anthony Volpe on the bubble as trade deadline nears: Where's he going? | KlapischJul. 31, 2026, 12:03 p.m.

On Saturday, the crowd at Citi Field, beaten down by months of bad baseball, came to life. They loved the video. It got the biggest cheer of the day.

Watching that video of themselves on the big Jumbotron screen in center field, I wonder how many of those Mets miss that summer of '86. I bet every single hand would be raised.

title: Padres' new-look rotation takes shape with Mize starting Wednesday and Ray on Friday
description: The San Diego Padres' new-look rotation is starting to take shape, with right-hander Casey Mize scheduled to start Wednesday against the Arizona Diamondbacks while lefty Robbie Ray will make his team debut Friday against the Houston Astros.  San Diego manager Craig Stammen said Tuesday it was good to have such quality reinforcements after the Padres were one of the trade deadline's big buyers.  San Diego came into Tuesday night's game against the Diamondbacks with a 58-55 record, two games behind Philadelphia and Arizona for the third National League wild card.
fullText:
PHOENIX (AP) — The San Diego Padres' new-look rotation is starting to take shape, with right-hander Casey Mize scheduled to start Wednesday against the Arizona Diamondbacks while lefty Robbie Ray will make his team debut Friday against the Houston Astros.

San Diego manager Craig Stammen said Tuesday it was good to have such quality reinforcements after the Padres were one of the trade deadline's big buyers. San Diego came into Tuesday night's game against the Diamondbacks with a 58-55 record, two games behind Philadelphia and Arizona for the third National League wild card.

"It's always nice to improve your roster and like (general manager) A.J. (Preller) says, we're here to try to win," Stammen said. "Adding those guys is a part of that process."

Mize had a 4-6 record with a 2.70 ERA through 16 starts with the Detroit Tigers this season despite managing a groin injury. Ray — the 2021 AL Cy Young Award winner — was 10-6 with a 3.08 ERA for the San Francisco Giants.

Mize said he knew there was a "50-50" chance he would be traded at Monday's deadline. He added that leaving the Tigers was emotional, but he's excited to join another quality organization.

"It wasn't like I was trying to get out of there — that place means a lot to me," Mize said. "But I couldn't be more excited and happy for this opportunity. I landed in a great situation. So some mixed emotions, but I'm happy with how everything turned out."

The Padres also hope veterans Joe Musgrove and Nick Pivetta will be able to rejoin the team's pitching staff soon. Both had a rehab outing Tuesday at Class A Lake Elsinore, with vastly different results.

Musgrove threw 2 2/3 innings, giving up one earned run and striking out three. The 33-year-old hasn't pitched in the big leagues since having Tommy John surgery in October 2024.

Pivetta threw just 14 pitches in relief before abruptly walking off the mound. Stammen said Pivetta experienced some tightness in his elbow, but recovered to throw a roughly 30-pitch bullpen in the batting cage a few minutes later.

"Take that for what it's worth — we'll find out how Nick feels tomorrow, same with Joe," Stammen said. "We'll find out how they feel tomorrow, reassess, then go on from there."

Pivetta went on the injured list April 14 because of elbow inflammation.

title: Akron Zips football is letting a fan script the opening drive of the home opener
description: One Akron season ticket holder will script the opening drive of the home opener.
fullText:
Forget the Playstation. If you ever wanted to be a college football coach, the University of Akron is giving someone the chance.

The school is giving one football season ticket holder a chance to help script the opening drive on offense for the Zips' home season opener against Robert Morris on Sept. 12 as part of a promotion announced Aug. 4.

Of course there's fine print, which reads, "With the head coach of course. This hasn't been done before but we're not crazy."

The promotion, called "Offensive Coordinator of the Game," will allow one randomly selected season ticket holder to work with Zips coach Joe Moorhead to design the plays for Akron's opening possession.

Moorhead said the winning fan will receive a behind-the-scenes look at the team's game-planning process.

"I'm looking forward to collaborating with the season ticket holder who wins this contest," Moorhead said in a statement. "This will give our fans a behind-the-scenes experience that has never been done before anywhere, so I'm excited to show them how to put together the opening script and see what they can do."

If you're curious, Akron hasn't scored a first drive touchdown in its home opener since 2022 — a 30-23 overtime win against St. Francis (Pa.).

Needless to say, some are having fun with it on X.

"Major props to Akron, this is one of the coolest season ticket giveaways I've ever seen," one tweet read.

If you're curious, season tickets for Zips football begin at $75.

Current Akron football season ticket holders are automatically entered into the drawing. Each season ticket counts as one entry, meaning fans with multiple season tickets receive additional entries.

Season ticket holders also can earn extra entries by referring new season ticket holders. Referrals can be made through the athletics ticket office or by including referral information when purchasing tickets.

The winner will be selected in a random drawing on Aug. 19 and will meet with Moorhead before the season opener to help script the team's opening drive.

This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: Akron Zips football is letting a fan script the opening drive of the home opener

title: Orioles defeat Angels behind a strong Cade Povich spot start, 3-1
description: The Birds surmounted an emotional trade deadline to beat a bad team and keep pace in the Wild Card race.
fullText:
So… here we are. The trade deadline has come and gone, and Adley Rutschman, Taylor Ward, Dean Kremer and Tyler Wells are no longer Orioles. MASN analyst Kevin Brown called it a "dark-hearted and depressing couple of days." Good for all the Birdland faithful still keeping a candle burning for this team—especially those of you who made it to the Yard a day after Monday's dramatic events. You're made of strong stuff.

Despite everything, there was still a game to be played. Tonight, it featured two former Orioles teammates, Cade Povich and current Angel Grayson Rodriguez, facing off on the mound. Neither has been good this year—Povich has mostly been in the minors, while Rodriguez entered this start with an ERA above seven. Yet somehow, of course, the two pitchers threw their best games of the year. In fact, for Rodriguez, it was his first quality start since July 2024… when he was an Oriole! (Does that make you feel good or bad?)

Still, a win is a win is a win. The Orioles scored two runs off Rodriguez, courtesy of a Pete Alonso single in the third, and Tyler O'Neill contributed a pinch-hit home run in the eighth to make it 3-1 Baltimore. That was enough, thanks to an unexpectedly strong Povich.

If you teleport back to the 2024 season, when the Orioles finished 91-71 and made it to the Wild Card series, you might remember that Rodriguez and Povich were rotation mates, along with Corbin Burnes, Albert Suárez, Cole Irvin and Dean Kremer. If you have a strong memory, you might remember that Rodriguez was good that year, making 20 starts and going 13-4 with a 3.86 ERA before getting shelved in July. G-Rod wouldn't throw a pitch as an Oriole again, missing all of 2025 and getting traded before the '26 season. Back in 2024, Cade Povich, meanwhile, made his MLB debut in June, then put up some terrible numbers, a 3-9 record with a 5.20 ERA and nearly four walks per game in his rookie season.

Consistency has bedeviled both of these starters since, but of the two former teammates, I must say Rodriguez looked stronger early on. Povich allowed five hits in three innings, stranding a pair of runners in the second and third innings both. It looked a bit dicey. As for Rodriguez, he struck out the first two O's swinging, then sat Baltimore hitters down in order in the second.

Then, suddenly, Rodriguez got (just for the span of one inning) hittable. It was a hiccup, but it was just enough for the O's to eke out the win.

That inning saw Orioles new guy Christian Franklin, a longtime Nationals farmhand, get a warm Oriole Park welcome in his very first MLB at-bat, then set up a run-scoring rally! Franklin walked, Colton Cowser singled, and Franklin chugged impressively from first to third. (Great game for the new guy, who also racked up his first stolen base in the seventh, and made a nice catch at the wall, too.) New catcher Carlos Narváez got aboard in his very first Orioles at-bat, too, getting hit by a pitch to load the bases with no outs. Rodriguez has struggled this season with runners in scoring position. He did again tonight, leaving a ball up for Pete Alonso, who hit a two-run single to center field. Franklin scored, so did Cowser. It was 2-0, O's.

At that point, it started to become apparent that Cade Povich was on some kind of a roll. He pitched a dominant fourth, fifth, and sixth innings. His pickoff game was astonishing. Povich allowed a leadoff walk in the fourth, picked off the runner and rung up the next two! In the fifth inning, Povich allowed only an infield single, then picked off the runner—his second of the night! A pair of flyballs and a bouncer to third wrapped up the sixth.

Ben McDonald described Povich as having "a slow heartbeat"—like a lizard, I guess? Well, tonight, the lefty, stashed in the Orioles minors since May, threw six scoreless with seven strikeouts. Even if the Orioles weren't down Chris Bassitt (to back problems) and Dean Kremer (to trade), this was a convincing audition for another turn in the rotation.

As for Povich's counterpart on the mound, if somehow what had you worried today was whether old Oriole friend Grayson Rodriguez would have a nice time in his return to Oriole Park, don't worry. O's hitters went down in order in five of seven innings tonight, scoring just the two runs on four hits, as Rodriguez completed seven innings—not just his first quality start of the year, but his first QS since July 2024, when he was an Oriole. Talk about a revenge glow-up. (Alternatively, this O's lineup may be bad.)

Three more innings to be played. How would this somewhat ransacked O's bullpen handle their responsibilities? Not gorgeously, but well enough!

In the seventh, Rico Garcia, lately hittable, allowed a Zach Neto deep flyball that nearly tied the game. Instead, new guy Christian Franklin reeled in at the wall.

Andrew Kittredge had a shaky eighth, allowing a run on a couple of strange plays. Contact hitter Nolan Schanuel hit a double, then scored on a ball booted by third baseman Christian Encarnación-Strand. (CES is in the lineup for his bat, let's say.) With two outs, Moisés Ballesteros hit a tapper back to the mound that Kittredge fielded, then hit Ballesteros in the back! But the home plate ump ruled the runner way out of the basepaths. So Kittredge was out of trouble.

Tyler O'Neill entered in the eighth as a pinch hitter, and got served a high fastball. Mr. Canada blasted it into the bullpen, giving his team a vital insurance run.

This made you feel a little better about Yennier Cano appearing as the closer. Though it wasn't a breeze for the newly-extend righty, who allowed a leadoff double, it was pretty good. Cano got a groundout, struck out Wade Meckler on a challenged strike call, and whiffed Zach Neto swinging.

"The Orioles needed this one," summed up the MASN booth after Cano got the save. As of this writing, the O's stand to gain ground in the Wild Card race, too, as Cleveland and Minnesota are both down in their respective games. Yeah. So maybe the Orioles aren't out of contention entirely. It doesn't fix all the vibes magically at once, but it's something.

So who is your Most Birdland Player of the night (and don't say Grayson Rodriguez)? Cade Povich, the little backup starter who could? Pete Alonso, author of the game-winning two-run single? Tyler O'Neill, big bopper in a pinch-hit role? New guy Christian Franklin, who walked, stole a base and scored a run in his MLB debut? Sound off about these, and all other matters, in the comments below.

title: Arraez has 2 hits and 2 RBIs in Phillies debut, Luzardo tosses 8 innings in 5-0 win over Nationals
description: Luis Arraez had two hits and two RBIs in his Philadelphia debut, Jesús Luzardo allowed four hits in eight innings and the Phillies beat the Washington Nationals 5-0 on Tuesday night for their fourth straight victory.  Trea Turner added three hits and an RBI for Philadelphia, which began play with a two-game cushion in the NL wild-card race.  The Phillies acquired Arraez, a three-time batting champion and four-time All-Star, from the San Francisco Giants for a pair of minor leaguers on Monday to help their powerful but strikeout-heavy lineup, and it paid dividends immediately.
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Luis Arraez had two hits and two RBIs in his Philadelphia debut, Jesús Luzardo allowed four hits in eight innings and the Phillies beat the Washington Nationals 5-0 on Tuesday night for their fourth straight victory.

Trea Turner added three hits and an RBI for Philadelphia, which began play with a two-game cushion in the NL wild-card race.

The Phillies acquired Arraez, a three-time batting champion and four-time All-Star, from the San Francisco Giants for a pair of minor leaguers on Monday to help their powerful but strikeout-heavy lineup, and it paid dividends immediately.

Batting fourth, Arraez drove in Turner from second base with an opposite-field single off Nationals opener Carson Palmquist (0-2) in the first to give Philadelphia a 1-0 lead and plated Turner again in Philadelphia's three-run third inning with a double to right field off Zack Littell.

That was plenty of run support for the All-Star lefty Luzardo (10-5), who struck out seven. Philadelphia improved to 46-18 in contests in which either Luzardo, Zack Wheeler or Cristopher Sánchez start.

The Phillies also had no problem defensively after making several shifts to their lineup to accommodate Arraez at second base, most notably moving two-time MVP Bryce Harper from first base to right field, where he had not played since April 13, 2022. Harper cleanly fielded the first pitch of the contest, retiring Dylan Crews on a line drive to right. Bryson Stott moved from second to third base, and Alec Bohm shifted from third to first base.

The reeling Nationals lost their seventh in a row. Already without Curtis Mead and Luis García Jr. after trading the run-producing hitters to the Red Sox and Yankees, respectively, Washington suffered a blow before the game by placing All-Star outfielder James Wood on the 10-day injured list with a strained left oblique.

Right-hander Caleb Kilian, whom the Phillies also got from the Giants in the Arraez trade, pitched a scoreless ninth.

Washington RHP Jake Irvin (2-5, 5.56) opposes Phillies RHP Andrew Painter (1-8, 6.72) in the third contest of the four-game set on Wednesday night.

title: Kirby Smart reveals when Georgia football will wear all-white uniforms
description: Kirby Smart surprised Georgia football players with the news that they will wear all-white uniforms for a game this season. Here's when they come out.
fullText:
Georgia football will be wearing all-white uniforms this season for one game.

Coach Kirby Smart revealed the news to the 2026 Bulldogs team on the eve of preseason camp.

Safety KJ Bolden and tight end Lawson Luckie were invited out during the team meeting wearing the white jerseys, white pants and white helmts with the black Georgia 'G' on the side.

Smart told the players the Bulldogs will wear them for the Sept. 12 12:45 p.m. home game against Western Kentucky, he said in a video posted Tuesday Aug. 4 to 'Glory Glory,' the subscriber NIL site.

Smart had told fans in the spring if they tripled subscriptions to the site by the spring game, the Bulldogs would wear the alternate uniforms.

Smart called out the players Tuesday under the guise of how players should dress and what they should wear for games.

"Ya'll been begging my ass," Smart said as the players turned up their volume in reaction to the unfiroms. "Hey, Hey. Hey. April Fools! April Fools! No, we're going to wear them Western Kentucky. Y'all have been begging for long enough. We're going to wear them one time and get them out there."

Georgia white uniforms have been seen during recruiting visits in recent years.

Georgia wore black jerseys twice in the 2020 season against Mississippi State in Athens and in the Peach Bowl against Cincinnati.

Now the all-whites are coming next month.

"I'm so sick of hearing about it," Smart said this spring laughing.

Free agent tight end Zach Ertz said in April that he didn't want his torn ACL to be the final act of his NFL career. He still is seeking an opportunity to make that wish come true.
